source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: 1 Samuel 1–16: all 406 public verses bind one-to-one to the matching original Hebrew records. Later chapters are outside this batch.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Keeps full ancestry and geographic identity while opening in two sentences.
verses.before: There was a certain man from Ramathaim-zophim, from the hill country of Ephraim, whose name was Elkanah, son of Jeroham, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, son of Zuph, an Ephraimite.
verses.after: There was a man from Ramathaim-zophim in the hill country of Ephraim. His name was Elkanah, son of Jeroham, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, son of Zuph, an Ephraimite.
verses.tsw_comparator: There was a certain man from Ramathaim-zophim, from the hill country of Ephraim, whose name was Elkanah, son of Jeroham, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, son of Zuph, an Ephraimite.

verses.rationale: Preserves contrast without evaluating either woman.
verses.before: He had two wives; the name of the one was Hannah, and the name of the other, Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children.
verses.after: He had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none.
verses.tsw_comparator: He had two wives; the name of the one was Hannah, and the name of the other, Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children.

verses.rationale: Preserves annual worship and introduces both priests by name.
verses.before: This man went up from his city year by year to worship and to sacrifice to the LORD of Hosts in Shiloh. Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were priests of the LORD there.
verses.after: Year after year this man went up from his town to worship and sacrifice to the LORD of Armies at Shiloh. Eli’s two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, served there as priests of the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: This man went up from his city year by year to worship and to sacrifice to the LORD of Hosts in Shiloh. Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were priests of the LORD there.

verses.rationale: Retains daughters as well as sons and recurring distribution.
verses.before: On the day when Elkanah sacrificed, he would give portions to Peninnah his wife and to all her sons and daughters.
verses.after: Whenever Elkanah offered a sacrifice, he gave portions to his wife Peninnah and to all her sons and daughters.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the day when Elkanah sacrificed, he would give portions to Peninnah his wife and to all her sons and daughters.

verses.rationale: Chooses double portion for obscure appayim, flagged in note; retains divine agency.
verses.before: But to Hannah he would give a double portion, because he loved Hannah, although the LORD had closed her womb.
verses.after: But he gave Hannah a double portion, because he loved her, though the LORD had closed her womb.
verses.tsw_comparator: But to Hannah he would give a double portion, because he loved Hannah, although the LORD had closed her womb.

verses.rationale: Preserves intentional distress and repeated womb statement.
verses.before: Her rival used to provoke her grievously to irritate her, because the LORD had closed her womb.
verses.after: Her rival kept provoking her, trying to upset her because the LORD had closed her womb.
verses.tsw_comparator: Her rival used to provoke her grievously to irritate her, because the LORD had closed her womb.

verses.rationale: Clarifies repeated annual situation and Hannah’s response.
verses.before: So it went on year after year, and as often as she went up to the house of the LORD, she was provoked; therefore, she wept and did not eat.
verses.after: This went on year after year. Whenever Hannah went up to the LORD’s house, her rival provoked her until she wept and would not eat.
verses.tsw_comparator: So it went on year after year, and as often as she went up to the house of the LORD, she was provoked; therefore, she wept and did not eat.

verses.rationale: Keeps four questions and ten rather than smoothing husband’s claim.
verses.before: Elkanah her husband said to her, "Hannah, why do you weep? Why do you not eat? Why is your heart sad? Am I not more to you than ten sons?"
verses.after: Her husband Elkanah said to her, “Hannah, why are you crying? Why will you not eat? Why is your heart so sad? Am I not better to you than ten sons?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Elkanah her husband said to her, "Hannah, why do you weep? Why do you not eat? Why is your heart sad? Am I not more to you than ten sons?"

verses.rationale: Avoids forcing Hannah herself to have eaten against preceding narrative; preserves sanctuary doorpost.
verses.before: After they had eaten and drunk in Shiloh, Hannah rose. Now Eli the priest was sitting on the chair by the doorpost of the temple of the LORD.
verses.after: After the eating and drinking at Shiloh, Hannah got up. Eli the priest was sitting on his chair beside the doorpost of the LORD’s sanctuary.
verses.tsw_comparator: After they had eaten and drunk in Shiloh, Hannah rose. Now Eli the priest was sitting on the chair by the doorpost of the temple of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains intensified weeping and inner bitterness.
verses.before: She was deeply distressed and prayed to the LORD and wept bitterly.
verses.after: Bitterly distressed, she prayed to the LORD and wept and wept.
verses.tsw_comparator: She was deeply distressed and prayed to the LORD and wept bitterly.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated servant, remember/not forget, lifetime and razor vow.
verses.before: She vowed a vow and said, "LORD of Hosts, if you will indeed look on the affliction of your maidservant and remember me and not forget your maidservant, but will give to your maidservant a son, then I will give him to the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor will touch his head."
verses.after: She made a vow: “LORD of Armies, if you will truly look on your servant’s suffering and remember me, if you will not forget your servant but give her a son, I will give him to the LORD for his whole life. No razor will touch his head.”
verses.tsw_comparator: She vowed a vow and said, "LORD of Hosts, if you will indeed look on the affliction of your maidservant and remember me and not forget your maidservant, but will give to your maidservant a son, then I will give him to the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor shall touch his head."

verses.rationale: Keeps duration and observation before misunderstanding.
verses.before: As she continued praying before the LORD, Eli observed her mouth.
verses.after: As she went on praying before the LORD, Eli watched her mouth.
verses.tsw_comparator: As she continued praying before the LORD, Eli observed her mouth.

verses.rationale: Preserves silent heart speech and observer’s mistaken inference.
verses.before: Hannah was speaking in her heart; only her lips moved, and her voice was not heard. Therefore Eli thought she was drunk.
verses.after: Hannah was speaking in her heart. Her lips moved, but no sound could be heard, so Eli thought she was drunk.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hannah was speaking in her heart; only her lips moved, and her voice was not heard. Therefore Eli thought she was drunk.

verses.rationale: Retains accusatory question and command.
verses.before: Eli said to her, "How long will you go on being drunk? Put your wine away from you."
verses.after: He said to her, “How long will you keep getting drunk? Put away your wine!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Eli said to her, "How long will you go on being drunk? Put your wine away from you."

verses.rationale: Preserves denial of both drinks and pouring-out image.
verses.before: Yet Hannah answered, "No, my lord, I am a woman troubled in spirit. I have neither drunk wine nor strong drink, but I have been pouring out my soul before the LORD.
verses.after: “No, my lord,” Hannah answered. “I am a woman in deep distress. I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink. I have been pouring out my soul before the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Hannah answered, "No, my lord, I am a woman troubled in spirit. I have neither drunk wine nor strong drink, but I have been pouring out my soul before the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps beliyyaal wording linking to Eli’s sons without adding diagnosis.
verses.before: Do not regard your maidservant as a worthless woman, for all along I have been speaking out of my great anxiety and vexation."
verses.after: Do not take your servant for a worthless woman. I have been speaking all this time out of my great anguish and grief.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not regard your maidservant as a worthless woman, for all along I have been speaking out of my great anxiety and vexation."

verses.rationale: Retains blessing rather than a guaranteed prediction.
verses.before: Then Eli answered, "Go in peace, and the God of Israel grant your petition that you have made to him."
verses.after: Eli replied, “Go in peace. May the God of Israel grant the request you have made of him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Eli answered, "Go in peace, and the God of Israel grant your petition that you have made to him."

verses.rationale: Makes changed expression natural without claiming all grief ended.
verses.before: And she said, "Let your maidservant find favor in your eyes." Then the woman went her way and ate, and her face was no longer sad.
verses.after: She said, “May your servant find favor with you.” Then the woman went on her way and ate. Her face was no longer downcast.
verses.tsw_comparator: And she said, "Let your maidservant find favor in your eyes." Then the woman went her way and ate, and her face was no longer sad.

verses.rationale: Keeps worship, intercourse and divine remembering distinct.
verses.before: They rose early in the morning and worshiped before the LORD; then they went back to their house at Ramah. And Elkanah knew Hannah his wife, and the LORD remembered her.
verses.after: They rose early the next morning, worshiped before the LORD, and returned home to Ramah. Elkanah slept with his wife Hannah, and the LORD remembered her.
verses.tsw_comparator: They rose early in the morning and worshiped before the LORD; then they went back to their house at Ramah. And Elkanah knew Hannah his wife, and the LORD remembered her.

verses.rationale: Retains naming explanation as wordplay rather than invented etymology.
verses.before: In due time, Hannah conceived and bore a son. She called his name Samuel, for she said, "I have asked for him from the LORD."
verses.after: In due time Hannah conceived and bore a son. She named him Samuel, saying, “I asked the LORD for him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: In due time, Hannah conceived and bore a son. She called his name Samuel, for she said, "I have asked for him from the LORD."

verses.rationale: Allows sentence to continue into Hannah’s contrast.
verses.before: The man Elkanah and all his house went up to offer to the LORD the annual sacrifice and to fulfill his vow,
verses.after: When Elkanah and his whole household went up to offer the annual sacrifice to the LORD and fulfill his vow,
verses.tsw_comparator: The man Elkanah and all his house went up to offer to the LORD the annual sacrifice and to fulfill his vow,

verses.rationale: Preserves delayed journey, weaning and permanent dedication.
verses.before: but Hannah did not go up, for she said to her husband, "As soon as the child is weaned, I will bring him, so that he may appear in the presence of the LORD and dwell there forever."
verses.after: Hannah did not go. She had told her husband, “Once the boy is weaned, I will bring him to appear before the LORD, and he will stay there for good.”
verses.tsw_comparator: but Hannah did not go up, for she said to her husband, "As soon as the child is weaned, I will bring him, so that he may appear in the presence of the LORD and dwell there forever."

verses.rationale: Keeps pinned his word rather than harmonizing to her vow.
verses.before: Elkanah her husband said to her, "Do what seems best to you; wait until you have weaned him; only, may LORD establish his word." So the woman remained and nursed her son until she weaned him.
verses.after: Her husband Elkanah said, “Do what seems right to you. Stay until you have weaned him. Only may the LORD establish his word.” So the woman stayed and nursed her son until she weaned him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Elkanah her husband said to her, "Do what seems best to you; wait until you have weaned him; only, may LORD establish his word." So the woman remained and nursed her son until she weaned him.

verses.rationale: Retains pinned three bulls despite next verse singular, with variant noted.
verses.before: When she had weaned him, she took him up with her, along with a three-year-old bull, an ephah of flour, and a skin of wine, and she brought him to the house of the LORD at Shiloh. And the child was young.
verses.after: When she had weaned him, she took him up with her, along with three bulls, one ephah of flour, and a skin of wine. She brought him to the LORD’s house at Shiloh while he was still very young.
verses.tsw_comparator: When she had weaned him, she took him up with her, along with a three-year-old bull, an ephah of flour, and a skin of wine, and she brought him to the house of the LORD at Shiloh. And the child was young.

verses.rationale: Preserves singular bull without harmonizing preceding three.
verses.before: They slaughtered the bull, and they brought the child to Eli.
verses.after: They slaughtered the bull and brought the boy to Eli.
verses.tsw_comparator: They slaughtered the bull, and they brought the child to Eli.

verses.rationale: Keeps appeal and recognition of earlier encounter.
verses.before: And she said, "O my lord, as you live, my lord, I am the woman who was standing here in your presence, praying to the LORD.
verses.after: She said, “Please, my lord—as surely as you live, I am the woman who stood here beside you praying to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: And she said, "O my lord, as you live, my lord, I am the woman who was standing here in your presence, praying to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains request repetition connecting name and answered prayer.
verses.before: For this child I prayed, and the LORD has granted me my petition that I made to him.
verses.after: I prayed for this boy, and the LORD granted the request I made of him.
verses.tsw_comparator: For this child I prayed, and the LORD has granted me my petition that I made to him.

verses.rationale: Retains lifetime dedication and unresolved masculine worshiper rather than changing to they.
verses.before: So I have lent him to the LORD. As long as he lives, he is lent to the LORD." And he worshiped the LORD there.
verses.after: Now I give him over to the LORD. For as long as he lives, he is given over to the LORD.” And he worshiped the LORD there.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I have lent him to the LORD. As long as he lives, he is lent to the LORD." And he worshiped the LORD there.

verses.rationale: Keeps horn and mouth imagery in verse-contained poetry, explaining horn selectively.
verses.before: Hannah prayed and said, “My heart exults in the LORD; my horn is lifted high in the LORD. My mouth is opened wide against my enemies, because I rejoice in your salvation.
verses.after: Hannah prayed: “My heart rejoices in the LORD; my horn is raised high in the LORD. My mouth opens wide against my enemies, for I rejoice in your deliverance.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Hannah prayed and said, “My heart exults in the LORD; my horn is lifted high in the LORD. My mouth is opened wide against my enemies, because I rejoice in your salvation.

verses.rationale: Retains switch to second-person address and rock image.
verses.before: There is none holy like the LORD, for there is none besides you; there is no rock like our God.
verses.after: No one is holy like the LORD. There is no one besides you; no rock is like our God.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is none holy like the LORD, for there is none besides you; there is no rock like our God.

verses.rationale: Keeps doubled pride wording and qere by him against ketiv not.
verses.before: Talk no more so very proudly, let not arrogance come from your mouth; for the LORD is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.
verses.after: Stop your lofty, lofty talk. Let no arrogance come from your mouths. The LORD is a God who knows, and by him deeds are weighed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Talk no more so very proudly, let not arrogance come from your mouth; for the LORD is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.

verses.rationale: Preserves reversals and strength as something girded on.
verses.before: The bows of the mighty are broken, but the feeble bind on strength.
verses.after: The bows of warriors are shattered, but those who stumbled put on strength.
verses.tsw_comparator: The bows of the mighty are broken, but the feeble bind on strength.

verses.rationale: Retains seven and poetic contrast without equating it with Hannah’s literal family count.
verses.before: People who were full have hired themselves out for bread, but people who were hungry have ceased to hunger; the barren has borne seven, but she who has many children languishes.
verses.after: Those once full hire themselves out for bread; those once hungry hunger no more. The woman who could not bear children has borne seven, but the mother of many grows feeble.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who were full have hired themselves out for bread, but those who were hungry have ceased to hunger; the barren has borne seven, but she who has many children languishes.

verses.rationale: Keeps death/life pair and ancient underworld term.
verses.before: The LORD kills and brings to life; he brings down to Sheol and raises up.
verses.after: The LORD kills and gives life; he brings down to Sheol and raises up.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD kills and brings to life; he brings down to Sheol and raises up.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated divine subject and opposed actions.
verses.before: The LORD makes poor and makes rich; he brings low and he exalts.
verses.after: The LORD makes poor and makes rich; he brings low and also lifts high.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD makes poor and makes rich; he brings low and he exalts.

verses.rationale: Keeps concrete poverty, throne and cosmological pillars images.
verses.before: He raises up the poor from the dust; he lifts the needy from the ash heap, to make them sit with princes and inherit a seat of honor. For the pillars of the earth are the LORD’s, and on them he has set the world.
verses.after: He raises the poor from the dust and lifts the needy from the ash heap, to seat them with nobles and give them a throne of honor. The pillars of the earth belong to the LORD; he has set the world upon them.
verses.tsw_comparator: He raises up the poor from the dust; he lifts the needy from the ash heap, to make them sit with princes and inherit a seat of honor. For the pillars of the earth are the LORD’s, and on them he has set the world.

verses.rationale: Follows qere plural faithful ones; keeps feet and darkness and the denial of strength as the basis of prevailing.
verses.before: He guards the feet of his faithful ones, but the wicked are cut off in darkness; for not by strength will a man prevail.
verses.after: He guards the feet of his faithful ones, but the wicked are silenced in darkness. For no one prevails by strength.
verses.tsw_comparator: He guards the feet of his faithful ones, but the wicked are cut off in darkness; for not by strength shall a man prevail.

verses.rationale: Preserves prospective king/anointed and horn link without naming later figure.
verses.before: People who contend with the LORD will be shattered; against them he will thunder in heaven. The LORD will judge the ends of the earth; he will give strength to his king and exalt the horn of his anointed.”
verses.after: Those who contend with the LORD will be shattered; he will thunder against them from heaven. The LORD will judge the ends of the earth. He will give strength to his king and raise high the horn of his anointed.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who contend with the LORD shall be shattered; against them he will thunder in heaven. The LORD will judge the ends of the earth; he will give strength to his king and exalt the horn of his anointed.”

verses.rationale: Makes contrast of father’s departure and boy’s service clear.
verses.before: Then Elkanah went home to Ramah. And the boy was ministering to the LORD in the presence of Eli the priest.
verses.after: Elkanah went home to Ramah. The boy stayed to serve the LORD under Eli the priest.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Elkanah went home to Ramah. And the boy was ministering to the LORD in the presence of Eli the priest.

verses.rationale: Keeps beliyyaal link to Hannah’s denial and knowing motif.
verses.before: Now the sons of Eli were worthless men; they did not know the LORD.
verses.after: Eli’s sons were worthless men. They did not know the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the sons of Eli were worthless men; they did not know the LORD.

verses.rationale: Identifies practice as conduct rather than valid legal entitlement.
verses.before: And the custom of the priests with the people was that when any man offered a sacrifice, the priest’s servant would come, while the meat was boiling, with a three-pronged fork in his hand,
verses.after: This was the priests’ practice with the people: whenever someone offered a sacrifice, the priest’s servant came with a three-pronged fork while the meat was boiling.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the custom of the priests with the people was that when any man offered a sacrifice, the priest’s servant would come, while the meat was boiling, with a three-pronged fork in his hand,

verses.rationale: Preserves four vessels and indiscriminate treatment.
verses.before: and he would thrust it into the pan or kettle or cauldron or pot; all that the fork brought up the priest would take for himself. Thus they did at Shiloh to all the Israelites who came there.
verses.after: He plunged it into the basin, kettle, cauldron, or pot, and the priest took whatever the fork brought up. This is what they did to all the Israelites who came to Shiloh.
verses.tsw_comparator: and he would thrust it into the pan or kettle or cauldron or pot; all that the fork brought up the priest would take for himself. Thus they did at Shiloh to all the Israelites who came there.

verses.rationale: Keeps violation’s timing and demand for raw meat.
verses.before: Moreover, before the fat was burned, the priest’s servant would come and say to the man who was sacrificing, “Give meat for the priest to roast, for he will not accept boiled meat from you, but only raw.”
verses.after: Even before the fat was burned, the priest’s servant would come and tell the person sacrificing, “Give the priest meat to roast. He will not accept boiled meat from you, only raw.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Moreover, before the fat was burned, the priest’s servant would come and say to the man who was sacrificing, “Give meat for the priest to roast, for he will not accept boiled meat from you, but only raw.”

verses.rationale: Follows qere no and preserves coercive threat.
verses.before: And if the man said to him, “Let them burn the fat first, and then take as much as you wish,” he would say, “No, but you will give it now, and if not, I will take it by force.”
verses.after: If the person said, “Let them burn the fat first; then take whatever you want,” the servant answered, “No. Give it now, or I will take it by force.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And if the man said to him, “Let them burn the fat first, and then take as much as you wish,” he would say, “No, but you shall give it now, and if not, I will take it by force.”

verses.rationale: Keeps gravity and direct contempt rather than shifting blame to worshipers.
verses.before: Thus the sin of the young men was very great in the sight of the LORD, for the men treated the offering of the LORD with contempt.
verses.after: The young men’s sin was very great before the LORD, for they treated the LORD’s offering with contempt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus the sin of the young men was very great in the sight of the LORD, for the men treated the offering of the LORD with contempt.

verses.rationale: Retains contrast and priestly garment without treating it as armor.
verses.before: Samuel was ministering before the LORD, a boy clothed with a linen ephod.
verses.after: Meanwhile Samuel served before the LORD, a boy wearing a linen ephod.
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel was ministering before the LORD, a boy clothed with a linen ephod.

verses.rationale: Keeps mother’s recurring act and annual visit.
verses.before: And his mother would make for him a little robe and bring it to him year by year, when she went up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.
verses.after: His mother made him a little robe and brought it up each year when she came with her husband to offer the annual sacrifice.
verses.tsw_comparator: And his mother would make for him a little robe and bring it to him year by year, when she went up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.

verses.rationale: Handles difficult asking/lending expression in context, preserving offspring and dedication.
verses.before: Then Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife, and say, “May the LORD give you children by this woman for the petition that she asked of the LORD.” So then they would return to their home.
verses.after: Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife: “May the LORD give you offspring through this woman in place of the one given over to the LORD.” Then they went home.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife, and say, “May the LORD give you children by this woman for the petition that she asked of the LORD.” So then they would return to their home.

verses.rationale: Retains five additional children and attention motif from Ruth.
verses.before: And the LORD visited Hannah, and she conceived and bore three sons and two daughters. And the boy Samuel grew in the presence of the LORD.
verses.after: The LORD attended to Hannah, and she conceived and bore three sons and two daughters. The boy Samuel grew up in the LORD’s presence.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD visited Hannah, and she conceived and bore three sons and two daughters. And the boy Samuel grew in the presence of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps sexual conduct and women’s service explicit, without inventing consent.
verses.before: Now Eli was very old, and he heard all that his sons were doing to all Israel, and how they lay with the women who served at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
verses.after: Eli was very old. He heard everything his sons were doing to all Israel, including how they slept with the women who served at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Eli was very old, and he heard all that his sons were doing to all Israel, and how they lay with the women who served at the entrance to the tent of meeting.

verses.rationale: Retains accusation and public reports.
verses.before: And he said to them, “Why do you do such things? For I hear of your evil dealings from all these people.
verses.after: He said to them, “Why are you doing these things? I hear reports of your evil deeds from all these people.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “Why do you do such things? For I hear of your evil dealings from all these people.

verses.rationale: Uses circulating-report reading of difficult maabirim, noting alternative causing transgression.
verses.before: No, my sons; for the report that I hear the people of the LORD spreading is not good.
verses.after: No, my sons. The report I hear circulating among the LORD’s people is not good.
verses.tsw_comparator: No, my sons; for the report that I hear the people of the LORD spreading is not good.

verses.rationale: Retains theological causal clause rather than reversing it; distinguishes mediation and prayer.
verses.before: If a man sins against a man, God will mediate for him; but if a man sins against the LORD, who can intercede for him?” But they did not listen to the voice of their father, for it was the will of the LORD to put them to death.
verses.after: If one person sins against another, God can intervene. But if someone sins against the LORD, who can intercede for them?” Yet they would not listen to their father, because the LORD intended to put them to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: If a man sins against a man, God will mediate for him; but if a man sins against the LORD, who can intercede for him?” But they did not listen to the voice of their father, for it was the will of the LORD to put them to death.

verses.rationale: Retains dual approval and continued growth.
verses.before: Now the boy Samuel continued to grow in stature and in favor with the LORD and also with men.
verses.after: The boy Samuel kept growing and gaining favor with both the LORD and people.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the boy Samuel continued to grow in stature and in favor with the LORD and also with men.

verses.rationale: Preserves two houses and rhetorical recall without naming unmentioned ancestor.
verses.before: And there came a man of God to Eli and said to him, “Thus says the LORD: Did I indeed reveal myself to the house of your father when they were in Egypt under the house of Pharaoh?
verses.after: A man of God came to Eli and said, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Did I not reveal myself to your father’s house when they were in Egypt, subject to Pharaoh’s house?
verses.tsw_comparator: And there came a man of God to Eli and said to him, “Thus says the LORD: Did I indeed reveal myself to the house of your father when they were in Egypt under the house of Pharaoh?

verses.rationale: Keeps priestly tasks and ancestral collective beneficiary.
verses.before: Did I choose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to go up to my altar, to burn incense, to wear an ephod before me? I gave to the house of your father all my offerings by fire from the people of Israel.
verses.after: I chose him from all Israel’s tribes to be my priest, to go up to my altar, burn incense, and wear an ephod before me. I gave your father’s house all the Israelites’ food offerings.

verses.rationale: Preserves god needing human replacement and facedown position.
verses.before: The Ashdodites rose early the next day, and look, Dagon had fallen upon his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD. So they took Dagon and returned him to his place.
verses.after: Early the next morning, the people of Ashdod found Dagon lying facedown on the ground before the LORD’s ark. They picked Dagon up and put him back in place.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Ashdodites rose early the next day, and look, Dagon had fallen upon his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD. So they took Dagon and returned him to his place.

verses.rationale: Uses contextual trunk for only Dagon remained, with difficulty noted.
verses.before: They rose early the next morning, and look, Dagon had fallen upon his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD. The head of Dagon and both palms of his hands were cut off upon the threshold; only Dagon’s trunk remained to him.
verses.after: Early the following morning, there was Dagon again, facedown before the LORD’s ark. His head and both hands had been cut off and lay on the threshold. Only his trunk remained.
verses.tsw_comparator: They rose early the next morning, and look, Dagon had fallen upon his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD. The head of Dagon and both palms of his hands were cut off upon the threshold; only Dagon’s trunk remained to him.

verses.rationale: Keeps narrator’s customary explanation and all entrants.
verses.before: So the priests of Dagon and everyone who enter the house of Dagon do not tread upon the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod to this day.
verses.after: That is why, to this day, neither Dagon’s priests nor anyone entering his temple in Ashdod steps on Dagon’s threshold.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore the priests of Dagon and all who enter the house of Dagon do not tread upon the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod to this day.

verses.rationale: Keeps heavy hand and broad tumor term without diagnosing plague.
verses.before: The hand of the LORD was heavy upon the Ashdodites, and he devastated them and struck them with tumors, Ashdod and its territories.
verses.after: The LORD’s hand lay heavy on the people of Ashdod. He devastated them and struck Ashdod and its surrounding territory with tumors.
verses.tsw_comparator: The hand of the LORD was heavy upon the Ashdodites, and he devastated them and struck them with tumors, Ashdod and its territories.

verses.rationale: Preserves their recognition of effects on people and god.
verses.before: When the men of Ashdod saw that it was so, they said, “The ark of the God of Israel will not remain with us, for his hand is harsh upon us and upon Dagon our god.”
verses.after: Seeing what was happening, the people of Ashdod said, “The ark of Israel’s God cannot stay with us. His hand is harsh against us and against Dagon our god.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When the men of Ashdod saw that it was so, they said, “The ark of the God of Israel shall not remain with us, for his hand is harsh upon us and upon Dagon our god.”

verses.rationale: Keeps collective decision and repeated object.
verses.before: So they sent and gathered to themselves all the rulers of the Philistines and said, “What will we do with the ark of the God of Israel?” They said, “Let the ark of the God of Israel be brought around to Gath.” So they brought around the ark of the God of Israel.
verses.after: They summoned all the Philistine rulers and asked, “What shall we do with the ark of Israel’s God?” The rulers answered, “Move it to Gath.” So they moved the ark of Israel’s God.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they sent and gathered to themselves all the rulers of the Philistines and said, “What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel?” They said, “Let the ark of the God of Israel be brought around to Gath.” So they brought around the ark of the God of Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserves inclusive small/great and uncertain outbreak verb without medical certainty.
verses.before: And it happened after they brought it around that the hand of the LORD was against the city with a very great panic. He struck the men of the city, from small to great, and tumors broke out upon them.
verses.after: After it was moved, the LORD’s hand struck the city with overwhelming panic. He struck its people, small and great, and tumors broke out on them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened after they brought it around that the hand of the LORD was against the city with a very great panic. He struck the men of the city, from small to great, and tumors broke out upon them.

verses.rationale: Retains collective singular voice in Ekron speech, explained in note.
verses.before: So they sent the ark of God to Ekron. And it happened when the ark of God came to Ekron that the Ekronites cried out, saying, “They have brought around the ark of the God of Israel to us to put us and our people to death!”
verses.after: Then they sent the ark of God to Ekron. As it arrived, the people of Ekron cried out, “They have brought the ark of Israel’s God to me to kill me and my people!”
verses.tsw_comparator: So they sent the ark of God to Ekron. And it happened when the ark of God came to Ekron that the Ekronites cried out, saying, “They have brought around the ark of the God of Israel to us to put us and our people to death!”

verses.rationale: Keeps singular communal voice and repeated heavy hand.
verses.before: So they sent and gathered all the rulers of the Philistines and said, “Send away the ark of the God of Israel, and let it return to its place, so that it does not put us and our people to death.” For there was a deadly panic throughout the whole city; the hand of God was very heavy there.
verses.after: They summoned all the Philistine rulers. “Send the ark of Israel’s God back where it belongs,” they said, “so it will not kill me and my people!” Deadly panic filled the city; God’s hand lay very heavy there.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they sent and gathered all the rulers of the Philistines and said, “Send away the ark of the God of Israel, and let it return to its place, so that it does not put us and our people to death.” For there was a deadly panic throughout the whole city; the hand of God was very heavy there.

verses.rationale: Preserves death/survivor contrast and ascending cry.
verses.before: The men who did not die were struck with tumors, and the cry of the city went up to the heavens.
verses.after: Those who did not die were struck with tumors, and the city’s cry for help rose to heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: The men who did not die were struck with tumors, and the cry of the city went up to the heavens.

verses.rationale: Retains exact duration.
verses.before: The ark of the LORD was in the territory of the Philistines seven months.
verses.after: The LORD’s ark remained in Philistine territory for seven months.
verses.tsw_comparator: The ark of the LORD was in the territory of the Philistines seven months.

verses.rationale: Keeps diviners and request about accompanying restitution.
verses.before: The Philistines called the priests and the diviners, saying, “What will we do with the ark of the LORD? Make known to us how we should send it to its place.”
verses.after: The Philistines summoned the priests and diviners. “What shall we do with the LORD’s ark?” they asked. “Tell us what to send with it when we return it to its place.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The Philistines called the priests and the diviners, saying, “What shall we do with the ark of the LORD? Make known to us how we should send it to its place.”

verses.rationale: Retains asham’s reparative function and hand question as counsel.
verses.before: They said, “If you send away the ark of the God of Israel, do not send it away empty, but surely return to him a guilt offering. Then you will be healed, and it will become known to you why his hand has not turned away from you.”
verses.after: They answered, “If you send back the ark of Israel’s God, do not send it empty. You must return a reparation offering to him. Then you will be healed and learn why his hand has not turned away from you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They said, “If you send away the ark of the God of Israel, do not send it away empty, but surely return to him a guilt offering. Then you will be healed, and it will become known to you why his hand has not turned away from you.”

verses.rationale: Keeps five plus five and representative rulers.
verses.before: They said, “What guilt offering will we return to him?” They said, “According to the number of the rulers of the Philistines: five gold tumors and five gold mice, for one plague was upon all of you and upon your rulers.
verses.after: “What reparation offering should we return?” they asked. “Five gold tumors and five gold mice,” came the answer, “one for each Philistine ruler. The same plague has struck all of you and your rulers.
verses.tsw_comparator: They said, “What guilt offering shall we return to him?” They said, “According to the number of the rulers of the Philistines: five gold tumors and five gold mice, for one plague was upon all of you and upon your rulers.

verses.rationale: Preserves tentative perhaps and honor/heavy-hand connection.
verses.before: So make images of your tumors and images of your mice that devastate the land, and give glory to the God of Israel. Perhaps he will lighten his hand from upon you, your gods, and your land.
verses.after: Make images of your tumors and of the mice ruining your land. Give honor to Israel’s God. Perhaps he will lighten his hand on you, your gods, and your land.
verses.tsw_comparator: So make images of your tumors and images of your mice that devastate the land, and give glory to the God of Israel. Perhaps he will lighten his hand from upon you, your gods, and your land.

verses.rationale: Keeps heart/heavy word network and Exodus recall.
verses.before: Why should you harden your heart as Egypt and Pharaoh hardened their heart? Was it not after he dealt severely with them that they sent them away, and they went?
verses.after: Why make your hearts heavy, as Egypt and Pharaoh made theirs? After he dealt harshly with them, did they not let the people go, and did the people not leave?
verses.tsw_comparator: Why should you harden your heart as Egypt and Pharaoh hardened their heart? Was it not after he dealt severely with them that they sent them away, and they went?

verses.rationale: Retains unyoked nursing cows and separation crucial to test.
verses.before: And now, take and prepare a new cart and two milk cows upon which no yoke has come. Yoke the cows to the cart, but take their calves home away from them.
verses.after: Now prepare a new cart and take two nursing cows that have never worn a yoke. Harness them to the cart, but take their calves away from them and keep them at home.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, take and prepare a new cart and two milk cows upon which no yoke has come. Yoke the cows to the cart, but take their calves home away from them.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes ark, box and offering.
verses.before: Take the ark of the LORD and put it on the cart. Put the gold objects that you return to him as a guilt offering in a box beside it, and send it away, and let it go.
verses.after: Put the LORD’s ark on the cart. Place the gold objects you are returning as a reparation offering in a box beside it. Then send it on its way.
verses.tsw_comparator: Take the ark of the LORD and put it on the cart. Put the gold objects that you return to him as a guilt offering in a box beside it, and send it away, and let it go.

verses.rationale: Retains experimental alternative and chance wording without narrator adjudication here.
verses.before: Then watch: if it goes up by the way of its own territory to Beth-Shemesh, he has done to us this great evil. But if not, then we will know that it was not his hand that struck us; it happened to us by chance.”
verses.after: Watch it. If it goes up toward its own territory, to Beth-shemesh, then he is the one who has brought this great disaster on us. If not, we will know his hand did not strike us; it happened to us by chance.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then watch: if it goes up by the way of its own territory to Beth-Shemesh, he has done to us this great evil. But if not, then we will know that it was not his hand that struck us; it happened to us by chance.”

verses.rationale: Keeps implementation matching instructions.
verses.before: The men did so. They took two milk cows and yoked them to the cart and shut up their calves at home.
verses.after: The men did this. They took two nursing cows, harnessed them to the cart, and shut their calves inside.
verses.tsw_comparator: The men did so. They took two milk cows and yoked them to the cart and shut up their calves at home.

verses.rationale: Preserves both kinds of objects.
verses.before: They put the ark of the LORD on the cart, with the box and the gold mice and the images of their tumors.
verses.after: They put the LORD’s ark on the cart, along with the box containing the gold mice and the images of their tumors.
verses.tsw_comparator: They put the ark of the LORD on the cart, with the box and the gold mice and the images of their tumors.

verses.rationale: Keeps lowing and unvarying route that matter to test.
verses.before: The cows went straight on the way toward Beth-Shemesh. They went on one highway, lowing as they went, and did not turn aside to the right or to the left. The rulers of the Philistines went after them as far as the border of Beth-Shemesh.
verses.after: The cows went straight along the road to Beth-shemesh. They stayed on one highway, lowing as they went, turning neither right nor left. The Philistine rulers followed them to the border of Beth-shemesh.
verses.tsw_comparator: The cows went straight on the way toward Beth-Shemesh. They went on one highway, lowing as they went, and did not turn aside to the right or to the left. The rulers of the Philistines went after them as far as the border of Beth-Shemesh.

verses.rationale: Retains wheat harvest and initial glad reception.
verses.before: Now the people of Beth-Shemesh were reaping the wheat harvest in the valley. They lifted their eyes and saw the ark, and they rejoiced to see it.
verses.after: The people of Beth-shemesh were harvesting wheat in the valley. When they looked up and saw the ark, they rejoiced at the sight.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the people of Beth-Shemesh were reaping the wheat harvest in the valley. They lifted their eyes and saw the ark, and they rejoiced to see it.

verses.rationale: Keeps named fieldowner distinct from earlier Joshua and reuse of cart.
verses.before: The cart came into the field of Joshua the Beth-Shemite and stood there. A great stone was there. They split the wood of the cart and offered the cows as a burnt offering to the LORD.
verses.after: The cart came into the field of Joshua of Beth-shemesh and stopped beside a large stone. They split up the cart’s wood and offered the cows as a burnt offering to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: The cart came into the field of Joshua the Beth-Shemite and stood there. A great stone was there. They split the wood of the cart and offered the cows as a burnt offering to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves Levites’ role and both sacrifice terms.
verses.before: The Levites took down the ark of the LORD and the box that was with it, in which were the gold objects, and put them upon the great stone. The men of Beth-Shemesh offered burnt offerings and sacrificed sacrifices that day to the LORD.
verses.after: The Levites took down the LORD’s ark and the box of gold objects beside it and set them on the large stone. That day the men of Beth-shemesh offered burnt offerings and sacrifices to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Levites took down the ark of the LORD and the box that was with it, in which were the gold objects, and put them upon the great stone. The men of Beth-Shemesh offered burnt offerings and sacrificed sacrifices that day to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains five witnesses and return date.
verses.before: When the five rulers of the Philistines saw it, they returned to Ekron that day.
verses.after: The five Philistine rulers watched, then returned to Ekron that same day.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the five rulers of the Philistines saw it, they returned to Ekron that day.

verses.rationale: Keeps five named city assignments with repeated one.
verses.before: These are the gold tumors that the Philistines returned as a guilt offering to the LORD: one for Ashdod, one for Gaza, one for Ashkelon, one for Gath, and one for Ekron.
verses.after: These were the gold tumors the Philistines returned to the LORD as a reparation offering: one for Ashdod, one for Gaza, one for Ashkelon, one for Gath, and one for Ekron.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the gold tumors that the Philistines returned as a guilt offering to the LORD: one for Ashdod, one for Gaza, one for Ashkelon, one for Gath, and one for Ekron.

verses.rationale: Uses contextual stone for difficult Abel and flags emendation rather than hiding it.
verses.before: And the gold mice were according to the number of all the cities of the Philistines belonging to the five rulers, from fortified city to unwalled village, as far as the great stone upon which they set down the ark of the LORD, which is in the field of Joshua the Beth-Shemite to this day.
verses.after: The gold mice corresponded to all the Philistine towns under the five rulers, from fortified cities to unwalled villages. The great stone where they set the LORD’s ark remains to this day in the field of Joshua of Beth-shemesh.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the gold mice were according to the number of all the cities of the Philistines belonging to the five rulers, from fortified city to unwalled village, as far as the great stone upon which they set down the ark of the LORD, which is in the field of Joshua the Beth-Shemite to this day.

verses.rationale: Combines both transmitted numbers without dropping fifty thousand; unusual source order and uncertainty recorded in note.
verses.before: But he struck some of the men of Beth-Shemesh because they looked into the ark of the LORD. He struck among the people seventy men, and the people mourned because the LORD had struck the people with a great slaughter.
verses.after: The LORD struck the men of Beth-shemesh because they looked into his ark. He struck down fifty thousand and seventy men. The people mourned because the LORD had dealt them such a heavy blow.
verses.tsw_comparator: But he struck some of the men of Beth-Shemesh because they looked into the ark of the LORD. He struck among the people seventy men, and the people mourned because the LORD had struck the people with a great slaughter.

verses.rationale: Keeps holy God and masculine he rather than flattening to ark alone.
verses.before: The men of Beth-Shemesh said, “Who can stand before the LORD, this holy God? And to whom will he go up from us?”
verses.after: The men of Beth-shemesh asked, “Who can stand before the LORD, this holy God? To whom will he go up, away from us?”
verses.tsw_comparator: The men of Beth-Shemesh said, “Who is able to stand before the LORD, this holy God? And to whom shall he go up from us?”

verses.rationale: Preserves invitation and geographic up/down.
verses.before: They sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath-Jearim, saying, “The Philistines have returned the ark of the LORD. Come down and bring it up to yourselves.”
verses.after: They sent messengers to the people of Kiriath-jearim: “The Philistines have returned the LORD’s ark. Come down and take it up to your town.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath-Jearim, saying, “The Philistines have returned the ark of the LORD. Come down and bring it up to yourselves.”

verses.rationale: Keeps location, father/son and specific guarding duty.
verses.before: The men of Kiriath-Jearim came and brought up the ark of the LORD. They brought it into the house of Abinadab on the hill and consecrated Eleazar his son to keep the ark of the LORD.
verses.after: The men of Kiriath-jearim came and took the LORD’s ark up to Abinadab’s house on the hill. They consecrated his son Eleazar to guard it.
verses.tsw_comparator: The men of Kiriath-Jearim came and brought up the ark of the LORD. They brought it into the house of Abinadab on the hill and consecrated Eleazar his son to keep the ark of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains twenty and difficult lament/longing verb without treating period as total ark residence.
verses.before: And it happened from the day the ark remained at Kiriath-Jearim that the days became many—twenty years—and all the house of Israel lamented after the LORD.
verses.after: A long time passed after the ark settled at Kiriath-jearim—twenty years. All the house of Israel lamented and longed for the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened from the day the ark remained at Kiriath-Jearim that the days became many—twenty years—and all the house of Israel lamented after the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps conditional return, exclusive service and hand rescue.
verses.before: Samuel spoke to all the house of Israel, saying, “If you are returning to the LORD with all your heart, remove the foreign gods and the Ashtaroth from your midst. Direct your heart to the LORD and serve him alone, and he will rescue you from the hand of the Philistines.”
verses.after: Samuel told all the house of Israel, “If you are returning to the LORD with all your heart, remove the foreign gods and the Ashtoreths from among you. Set your hearts on the LORD and serve him alone. Then he will rescue you from the Philistines’ hand.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel spoke to all the house of Israel, saying, “If you are returning to the LORD with all your heart, remove the foreign gods and the Ashtaroth from your midst. Direct your heart to the LORD and serve him alone, and he will rescue you from the hand of the Philistines.”

verses.rationale: Retains both named plural deities and enacted response.
verses.before: So the children of Israel removed the Baals and the Ashtaroth and served the LORD alone.
verses.after: The Israelites removed the Baals and the Ashtoreths and served the LORD alone.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the children of Israel removed the Baals and the Ashtaroth and served the LORD alone.

verses.rationale: Keeps gathering and intercession connected.
verses.before: Samuel said, “Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray to the LORD for you.”
verses.after: Samuel said, “Gather all Israel at Mizpah, and I will pray to the LORD for you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel said, “Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray to the LORD for you.”

verses.rationale: Retains water ritual without inventing its meaning and judge role.
verses.before: They gathered at Mizpah, drew water and poured it out before the LORD, and fasted on that day. They said there, “We have sinned against the LORD.” And Samuel judged the children of Israel at Mizpah.
verses.after: They gathered at Mizpah, drew water, and poured it out before the LORD. They fasted that day and said, “We have sinned against the LORD.” Samuel judged the Israelites at Mizpah.
verses.tsw_comparator: They gathered at Mizpah, drew water and poured it out before the LORD, and fasted on that day. They said there, “We have sinned against the LORD.” And Samuel judged the children of Israel at Mizpah.

verses.rationale: Keeps mirrored hearing and response.
verses.before: When the Philistines heard that the children of Israel had gathered at Mizpah, the rulers of the Philistines went up against Israel. When the children of Israel heard, they were afraid before the Philistines.
verses.after: When the Philistines heard that the Israelites had gathered at Mizpah, their rulers advanced against Israel. The Israelites heard and were afraid of them.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the Philistines heard that the children of Israel had gathered at Mizpah, the rulers of the Philistines went up against Israel. When the children of Israel heard, they were afraid before the Philistines.

verses.rationale: Preserves ongoing plea rather than single prayer request.
verses.before: The children of Israel said to Samuel, “Do not be silent from crying out for us to the LORD our God, that he may save us from the hand of the Philistines.”
verses.after: They said to Samuel, “Do not stop crying out to the LORD our God for us, so he may save us from the Philistines’ hand.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The children of Israel said to Samuel, “Do not be silent from crying out for us to the LORD our God, that he may save us from the hand of the Philistines.”

verses.rationale: Retains nursing lamb, whole offering and answered cry.
verses.before: Samuel took one nursing lamb and offered it whole as a burnt offering to the LORD. Samuel cried out to the LORD for Israel, and the LORD answered him.
verses.after: Samuel took a nursing lamb and offered it whole as a burnt offering to the LORD. He cried out to the LORD for Israel, and the LORD answered him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel took one nursing lamb and offered it whole as a burnt offering to the LORD. Samuel cried out to the LORD for Israel, and the LORD answered him.

verses.rationale: Keeps simultaneity and thunder link to Hannah’s poem.
verses.before: As Samuel was offering the burnt offering, the Philistines drew near for battle against Israel. But the LORD thundered with a great voice on that day against the Philistines and threw them into confusion, and they were struck before Israel.
verses.after: While Samuel was offering the burnt offering, the Philistines drew near to fight Israel. That day the LORD thundered loudly against them, threw them into confusion, and they were defeated before Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: As Samuel was offering the burnt offering, the Philistines drew near for battle against Israel. But the LORD thundered with a great voice on that day against the Philistines and threw them into confusion, and they were struck before Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains pursuit endpoint and below qualifier.
verses.before: The men of Israel went out from Mizpah and pursued the Philistines and struck them as far as below Beth-Car.
verses.after: The men of Israel came out from Mizpah and pursued the Philistines, striking them down as far as below Beth-car.
verses.tsw_comparator: The men of Israel went out from Mizpah and pursued the Philistines and struck them as far as below Beth-Car.

verses.rationale: Preserves stone/name explanation and temporal/spatial openness of thus far.
verses.before: Then Samuel took a stone and set it between Mizpah and Shen and called its name Ebenezer. He said, “Thus far the LORD has helped us.”
verses.after: Samuel took a stone and set it between Mizpah and Shen. He named it Ebenezer, saying, “Thus far the LORD has helped us.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Samuel took a stone and set it between Mizpah and Shen and called its name Ebenezer. He said, “Thus far the LORD has helped us.”

verses.rationale: Keeps narrator’s sweeping summary without harmonizing later conflicts.
verses.before: So the Philistines were subdued and did not again enter the territory of Israel. The hand of the LORD was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.
verses.after: The Philistines were subdued and stopped entering Israel’s territory. The LORD’s hand was against them throughout Samuel’s days.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the Philistines were subdued and did not again enter the territory of Israel. The hand of the LORD was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.

verses.rationale: Preserves territorial recovery and separate Amorite peace.
verses.before: The cities that the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored to Israel, from Ekron as far as Gath, and Israel rescued their territory from the hand of the Philistines. And there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.
verses.after: The towns the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored, from Ekron to Gath. Israel also rescued their surrounding territory from the Philistines’ hand. There was peace between Israel and the Amorites.
verses.tsw_comparator: The cities that the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored to Israel, from Ekron as far as Gath, and Israel rescued their territory from the hand of the Philistines. And there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.

verses.rationale: Retains lifetime judicial summary.
verses.before: Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.
verses.after: Samuel judged Israel throughout his life.
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.

verses.rationale: Keeps annual circuit and all three sites.
verses.before: He went year by year in circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah, and he judged Israel at all these places.
verses.after: Each year he traveled a circuit through Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah, judging Israel in all these places.
verses.tsw_comparator: He went year by year in circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah, and he judged Israel at all these places.

verses.rationale: Retains home, judging and altar at same location.
verses.before: Then he returned to Ramah, for his house was there, and there he judged Israel. And he built there an altar to the LORD.
verses.after: He always returned to Ramah, where his home was. He judged Israel there too, and there he built an altar to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he returned to Ramah, for his house was there, and there he judged Israel. And he built there an altar to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps aging and appointment as narrative cause.
verses.before: And it happened when Samuel became old that he appointed his sons as judges over Israel.
verses.after: When Samuel grew old, he appointed his sons as judges over Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened when Samuel became old that he appointed his sons as judges over Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserves birth order, names and location.
verses.before: The name of his firstborn son was Joel, and the name of his second Abijah. They were judges in Beersheba.
verses.after: His firstborn was named Joel and his second son Abijah. They judged at Beersheba.
