verses.after: The LORD’s Spirit will rush upon you. You will prophesy with them and become a different man.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the Spirit of the LORD will rush upon you, and you will prophesy with them and be turned into another man.

verses.rationale: Keeps hand idiom without turning it into unlimited future permission.
verses.before: And it will be when these signs come to you, do for yourself what your hand finds, for God is with you.
verses.after: When these signs happen to you, do whatever your hand finds to do, for God is with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it shall be when these signs come to you, do for yourself what your hand finds, for God is with you.

verses.rationale: Retains seven-day wait until arrival and both offerings.
verses.before: Then go down before me to Gilgal. Look, I will come down to you to offer burnt offerings and sacrifice offerings of well-being. Seven days you will wait until I come to you and reveal to you what you will do.”
verses.after: Go down ahead of me to Gilgal. I will come down to you to offer burnt offerings and sacrifices of well-being. Wait seven days, until I come and tell you what to do.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then go down before me to Gilgal. Look, I will come down to you to offer burnt offerings and sacrifice offerings of well-being. Seven days you shall wait until I come to you and make known to you what you shall do.”

verses.rationale: Keeps divine heart transformation and same-day fulfillment.
verses.before: And it happened when he turned his shoulder to go from Samuel that God changed his heart into another, and all these signs came that day.
verses.after: As Saul turned to leave Samuel, God changed his heart, and all these signs happened that day.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened when he turned his shoulder to go from Samuel that God changed his heart into another, and all these signs came that day.

verses.rationale: Preserves Spirit of God wording and meeting.
verses.before: They came there to Gibeah, and look, a band of prophets came to meet him. Then the Spirit of God rushed upon him, and he prophesied in their midst.
verses.after: When they reached Gibeah, a band of prophets met him. God’s Spirit rushed upon him, and he prophesied among them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They came there to Gibeah, and look, a band of prophets came to meet him. Then the Spirit of God rushed upon him, and he prophesied in their midst.

verses.rationale: Keeps prior acquaintance, father identification and proverb question.
verses.before: And it happened when everyone who had known him before saw that, look, he prophesied with prophets, the people said each to his companion, “What is this that has happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?”
verses.after: Everyone who had known him before saw him prophesying with the prophets. They asked one another, “What has happened to Kish’s son? Is Saul among the prophets too?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened when everyone who had known him before saw that, behold, he prophesied with prophets, the people said each to his companion, “What is this that has happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?”

verses.rationale: Retains enigmatic father question without asserting hereditary or prophetic-school meaning.
verses.before: A man from there answered and said, “And who is their father?” Therefore it became a proverb, “Is Saul also among the prophets?”
verses.after: A man from there answered, “And who is their father?” So it became a saying: “Is Saul among the prophets too?”
verses.tsw_comparator: A man from there answered and said, “And who is their father?” Therefore it became a proverb, “Is Saul also among the prophets?”

verses.rationale: Keeps high place rather than harmonizing to home.
verses.before: When he finished prophesying, he came to the high place.
verses.after: When Saul finished prophesying, he went to the high place.
verses.tsw_comparator: When he finished prophesying, he came to the high place.

verses.rationale: Preserves uncle addressing both and Saul’s report.
verses.before: Saul’s uncle said to him and to his young man, “Where did you go?” He said, “To seek the donkeys. When we saw that they were not found, we went to Samuel.”
verses.after: Saul’s uncle asked him and his servant, “Where did you go?” Saul answered, “To look for the donkeys. When we saw they were nowhere to be found, we went to Samuel.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul’s uncle said to him and to his young man, “Where did you go?” He said, “To seek the donkeys. When we saw that they were not found, we went to Samuel.”

verses.rationale: Retains renewed request for disclosure.
verses.before: Saul’s uncle said, “Please tell me what Samuel said to you.”
verses.after: His uncle said, “Please tell me what Samuel said to you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul’s uncle said, “Please tell me what Samuel said to you.”

verses.rationale: Keeps deliberate partial disclosure without inventing motive.
verses.before: Saul said to his uncle, “He told us plainly that the donkeys had been found.” But the matter of the kingship, of which Samuel had spoken, he did not tell him.
verses.after: Saul told him, “He assured us that the donkeys had been found.” But he did not tell his uncle what Samuel had said about the kingship.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul said to his uncle, “He told us plainly that the donkeys had been found.” But the matter of the kingship, of which Samuel had spoken, he did not tell him.

verses.rationale: Preserves religious purpose and gathering site.
verses.before: Samuel called the people together to the LORD at Mizpah.
verses.after: Samuel summoned the people to the LORD at Mizpah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel called the people together to the LORD at Mizpah.

verses.rationale: Keeps first-person divine rescue and repeated hand.
verses.before: He said to the children of Israel, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: I brought Israel up from Egypt, and I rescued you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all the kingdoms that oppressed you.
verses.after: He told the Israelites, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘I brought Israel up from Egypt. I rescued you from Egypt’s hand and from the hand of every kingdom that oppressed you.’
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to the children of Israel, “Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: I brought Israel up from Egypt, and I rescued you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all the kingdoms that oppressed you.

verses.rationale: Retains rejection accusation and ordered selection units.
verses.before: But today you have rejected your God, who himself saves you from all your evils and your distresses, and you have said to him, ‘No, but set a king over us.’ And now present yourselves before the LORD by your tribes and by your clans.”
verses.after: But today you have rejected your God, who saves you from all your disasters and distress. You have said to him, ‘Appoint a king over us.’ Now take your places before the LORD by tribes and clans.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But today you have rejected your God, who himself saves you from all your evils and your distresses, and you have said to him, ‘No, but set a king over us.’ And now present yourselves before the LORD by your tribes and by your clans.”

verses.rationale: Keeps chosen passive without adding mechanism beyond source.
verses.before: Samuel brought all the tribes of Israel near, and the tribe of Benjamin was taken.
verses.after: Samuel brought all Israel’s tribes forward, and Benjamin’s tribe was chosen.
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel brought all the tribes of Israel near, and the tribe of Benjamin was taken.

verses.rationale: Preserves clan and person selection with sudden absence.
verses.before: He brought the tribe of Benjamin near by its clans, and the clan of the Matrites was taken, and Saul son of Kish was taken. But when they sought him, he could not be found.
verses.after: He brought Benjamin’s tribe forward by clans, and the Matrite clan was chosen. Then Saul son of Kish was chosen. They looked for him but could not find him.
verses.tsw_comparator: He brought the tribe of Benjamin near by its clans, and the clan of the Matrites was taken, and Saul son of Kish was taken. But when they sought him, he could not be found.

verses.rationale: Keeps inquiry and hidden location without inferring fear.
verses.before: So they inquired again of the LORD, “Has the man come here yet?” The LORD said, “Look, he has hidden himself among the baggage.”
verses.after: They inquired of the LORD again, “Has the man come here yet?” The LORD answered, “He is hiding among the baggage.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So they inquired again of the LORD, “Has the man come here yet?” The LORD said, “Look, he has hidden himself among the baggage.”

verses.rationale: Retains retrieval and repeated height motif.
verses.before: They ran and took him from there. He stood among the people, and he was taller than all the people from his shoulders upward.
verses.after: They ran and brought him from there. As he stood among the people, he was a head taller than all of them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They ran and took him from there. He stood in the midst of the people, and he was taller than all the people from his shoulders upward.

verses.rationale: Keeps Samuel’s assessment and popular acclaim.
verses.before: Samuel said to all the people, “Do you see the one whom the LORD has chosen? For there is none like him among all the people.” And all the people shouted and said, “Long live the king!”
verses.after: Samuel said to all the people, “Do you see the one the LORD has chosen? There is no one like him among all the people.” They all shouted, “Long live the king!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel said to all the people, “Do you see the one whom the LORD has chosen? For there is none like him among all the people.” And all the people shouted and said, “Long live the king!”

verses.rationale: Keeps mishpat of kingship distinct from warning about king’s practice in chapter 8.
verses.before: Samuel spoke to the people the judgment of the kingship and wrote it in a book and placed it before the LORD. Then Samuel sent all the people away, each man to his house.
verses.after: Samuel explained the provisions of kingship to the people, wrote them in a scroll, and placed it before the LORD. Then he sent everyone home.
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel spoke to the people the judgment of the kingship and wrote it in a book and placed it before the LORD. Then Samuel sent all the people away, each man to his house.

verses.rationale: Retains divine touching and supportive men without inventing standing army.
verses.before: Saul also went to his house at Gibeah, and with him went the valiant men whose hearts God had touched.
verses.after: Saul also went home to Gibeah. A band of capable men whose hearts God had touched went with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul also went to his house at Gibeah, and with him went the valiant men whose hearts God had touched.

verses.rationale: Follows pinned silent ending, with longer transition witnesses identified only if verified.
verses.before: But worthless men said, “How can this one save us?” They despised him and did not bring him a gift. But he was as one who kept silent.
verses.after: But some worthless men said, “How can this fellow save us?” They despised him and brought him no gift. Saul kept silent.
verses.tsw_comparator: But worthless men said, “How can this one save us?” They despised him and did not bring him a gift. But he was as one who kept silent.

verses.rationale: Keeps siege, covenant and offered subjection.
verses.before: Nahash the Ammonite went up and camped against Jabesh-Gilead. All the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, “Make a covenant with us, and we will serve you.”
verses.after: Nahash the Ammonite came up and laid siege to Jabesh-gilead. All the men of Jabesh said to him, “Make a covenant with us, and we will serve you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Nahash the Ammonite went up and camped against Jabesh-Gilead. All the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, “Make a covenant with us, and we will serve you.”

verses.rationale: Preserves specific mutilation and collective humiliation.
verses.before: Nahash the Ammonite said to them, “On this condition I will make it with you: by gouging out every right eye of yours, and I will make it a reproach upon all Israel.”
verses.after: Nahash the Ammonite answered, “I will make it on this condition: I gouge out every one of your right eyes and bring disgrace on all Israel.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Nahash the Ammonite said to them, “On this condition I will make it with you: by gouging out every right eye of yours, and I will make it a reproach upon all Israel.”

verses.rationale: Retains seven-day reprieve and conditional surrender.
verses.before: The elders of Jabesh said to him, “Give us seven days’ respite so that we may send messengers throughout all the territory of Israel. Then if there is no one to save us, we will come out to you.”
verses.after: The elders of Jabesh said, “Give us seven days to send messengers throughout Israel. If no one saves us, we will come out to you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The elders of Jabesh said to him, “Give us seven days’ respite so that we may send messengers throughout all the territory of Israel. Then if there is no one to save us, we will come out to you.”

verses.rationale: Keeps location and communal response.
verses.before: The messengers came to Gibeah of Saul and spoke the words in the ears of the people. All the people lifted their voices and wept.
verses.after: The messengers reached Gibeah of Saul and reported this in the people’s hearing. Everyone wept aloud.
verses.tsw_comparator: The messengers came to Gibeah of Saul and spoke the words in the ears of the people. All the people lifted their voices and wept.

verses.rationale: Preserves king still returning from agricultural work.
verses.before: And look, Saul was coming after the cattle from the field. Saul said, “What is with the people that they are weeping?” So they recounted to him the words of the men of Jabesh.
verses.after: Just then Saul came in from the field behind the cattle. “What is wrong with the people? Why are they crying?” he asked. They told him what the men of Jabesh had said.
verses.tsw_comparator: And look, Saul was coming after the cattle from the field. Saul said, “What is with the people that they are weeping?” So they recounted to him the words of the men of Jabesh.

verses.rationale: Keeps hearing, Spirit and anger sequence.
verses.before: The Spirit of God rushed upon Saul when he heard these words, and his anger burned greatly.
verses.after: When Saul heard these words, God’s Spirit rushed upon him, and he burned with anger.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Spirit of God rushed upon Saul when he heard these words, and his anger burned greatly.

verses.rationale: Preserves coercive summons, animal dismemberment and divine terror without endorsing method.
verses.before: He took a pair of oxen, cut them into pieces, and sent them throughout all the territory of Israel by the hand of messengers, saying, “Whoever does not come out after Saul and after Samuel, thus will it be done to his oxen.” Then the dread of the LORD fell upon the people, and they came out as one man.
verses.after: He took a pair of oxen, cut them in pieces, and sent the pieces by messengers throughout Israel: “This is what will be done to the cattle of anyone who does not come out after Saul and Samuel.” Terror from the LORD fell on the people, and they came out as one man.
verses.tsw_comparator: He took a pair of oxen, cut them into pieces, and sent them throughout all the territory of Israel by the hand of messengers, saying, “Whoever does not come out after Saul and after Samuel, thus shall it be done to his oxen.” Then the dread of the LORD fell upon the people, and they came out as one man.

verses.rationale: Retains separate totals and place.
verses.before: He mustered them at Bezek. The children of Israel were three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand.
verses.after: He mustered them at Bezek: three hundred thousand Israelites and thirty thousand men of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: He mustered them at Bezek. The children of Israel were three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand.

verses.rationale: Keeps next-day timing and rescue promise.
verses.before: They said to the messengers who had come, “Thus you will say to the men of Jabesh-Gilead: ‘Tomorrow there will be salvation for you when the sun is hot.’” The messengers came and told the men of Jabesh, and they rejoiced.
verses.after: They told the messengers who had come, “Tell the men of Jabesh-gilead: ‘Tomorrow, by the heat of the sun, you will be rescued.’” The messengers returned with the news, and the men of Jabesh rejoiced.
verses.tsw_comparator: They said to the messengers who had come, “Thus you shall say to the men of Jabesh-Gilead: ‘Tomorrow there will be salvation for you when the sun is hot.’” The messengers came and told the men of Jabesh, and they rejoiced.

verses.rationale: Preserves deceptive surrender language without explaining plan in speech.
verses.before: The men of Jabesh said, “Tomorrow we will come out to you, and you may do to us whatever is good in your eyes.”
verses.after: The men of Jabesh told the Ammonites, “Tomorrow we will come out to you, and you may do whatever seems good to you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The men of Jabesh said, “Tomorrow we will come out to you, and you may do to us whatever is good in your eyes.”

verses.rationale: Keeps three companies, time span and scattered pairs.
verses.before: And it happened the next day that Saul placed the people in three companies. They came into the midst of the camp during the morning watch and struck Ammon until the heat of the day. People who remained were scattered, so that no two of them were left together.
verses.after: The next day Saul divided the troops into three companies. They entered the Ammonite camp during the morning watch and struck them down until the heat of the day. The survivors scattered so completely that no two remained together.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened the next day that Saul placed the people in three companies. They came into the midst of the camp during the morning watch and struck Ammon until the heat of the day. Those who remained were scattered, so that no two of them were left together.

verses.rationale: Retains retaliatory demand and challenge to kingship.
verses.before: Then the people said to Samuel, “Who is the one who said, ‘Will Saul reign over us?’ Give the men, and we will put them to death.”
verses.after: The people said to Samuel, “Who was it that said, ‘Will Saul reign over us?’ Hand those men over so we can put them to death.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the people said to Samuel, “Who is the one who said, ‘Shall Saul reign over us?’ Give the men, and we will put them to death.”

verses.rationale: Keeps reprieve limited to today and divine credit.
verses.before: Yet Saul said, “No man will be put to death on this day, for today the LORD has worked salvation in Israel.”
verses.after: But Saul said, “No one will be put to death today. Today the LORD has brought deliverance to Israel.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Saul said, “No man shall be put to death on this day, for today the LORD has worked salvation in Israel.”

verses.rationale: Preserves renewal rather than first appointment.
verses.before: Samuel said to the people, “Come, let us go to Gilgal and renew the kingship there.”
verses.after: Samuel told the people, “Come, let us go to Gilgal and renew the kingship there.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel said to the people, “Come, let us go to Gilgal and renew the kingship there.”

verses.rationale: Keeps public kingship, offerings and celebration.
verses.before: So all the people went to Gilgal, and there they made Saul king before the LORD at Gilgal. There they sacrificed offerings of well-being before the LORD, and there Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly.
verses.after: Everyone went to Gilgal. There, before the LORD, they made Saul king and offered sacrifices of well-being. Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly there.
verses.tsw_comparator: So all the people went to Gilgal, and there they made Saul king before the LORD at Gilgal. There they sacrificed offerings of well-being before the LORD, and there Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly.

verses.rationale: Preserves listening and fulfillment of request.
verses.before: Samuel said to all Israel, “See, I have listened to your voice in all that you said to me, and I have set a king over you.
verses.after: Samuel said to all Israel, “I have listened to everything you asked of me and appointed a king over you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel said to all Israel, “See, I have listened to your voice in all that you said to me, and I have set a king over you.

verses.rationale: Keeps walk-before repetition linking leaders and sons’ presence.
verses.before: And now, see, the king walks before you, and I am old and gray; and see, my sons are with you. I have walked before you from my youth until this day.
verses.after: Now the king walks before you. I have grown old and gray, and my sons are here among you. I have walked before you from my youth until this day.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, see, the king walks before you, and I am old and gray; and see, my sons are with you. I have walked before you from my youth until this day.

verses.rationale: Retains questions echoing taking king and offer of restitution.
verses.before: Here I am. Testify against me before the LORD and before his anointed. Whose ox have I taken? Whose donkey have I taken? Whom have I defrauded? Whom have I oppressed? From whose hand have I taken a bribe to blind my eyes with it? I will restore it to you.”
verses.after: Here I am. Testify against me before the LORD and his anointed: whose ox have I taken? Whose donkey have I taken? Whom have I exploited or oppressed? From whose hand have I taken a bribe to shut my eyes? I will repay you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Here I am. Testify against me before the LORD and before his anointed. Whose ox have I taken? Whose donkey have I taken? Whom have I defrauded? Whom have I oppressed? From whose hand have I taken a bribe to blind my eyes with it? I will restore it to you.”

verses.rationale: Keeps public exoneration in people’s speech.
verses.before: They said, “You have not defrauded us or oppressed us or taken anything from anyone’s hand.”
verses.after: They answered, “You have not exploited or oppressed us. You have taken nothing from anyone.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They said, “You have not defrauded us or oppressed us or taken anything from anyone’s hand.”

verses.rationale: Preserves collective reply without forcing singular source verb’s speaker.
verses.before: He said to them, “The LORD is witness against you, and his anointed is witness this day, that you have found nothing in my hand.” And they said, “He is witness.”
verses.after: He said, “The LORD is witness against you today, and his anointed is witness, that you have found nothing in my hand.” “He is witness,” came the answer.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to them, “The LORD is witness against you, and his anointed is witness this day, that you have found nothing in my hand.” And they said, “He is witness.”

verses.rationale: Keeps divine actor and both leaders.
verses.before: Then Samuel said to the people, “The LORD is witness, who appointed Moses and Aaron and brought your ancestors up from the land of Egypt.
verses.after: Samuel continued, “It was the LORD who appointed Moses and Aaron and brought your ancestors up from Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Samuel said to the people, “The LORD is witness, who appointed Moses and Aaron and brought your ancestors up from the land of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Preserves legal dispute frame and righteous acts.
verses.before: Now therefore stand still, so that I may plead with you before the LORD concerning all the righteous acts of the LORD that he did for you and for your ancestors.
verses.after: Now stand here while I lay the case before you in the LORD’s presence: all the righteous acts the LORD has done for you and your ancestors.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now therefore stand still, so that I may plead with you before the LORD concerning all the righteous acts of the LORD that he did for you and for your ancestors.

verses.rationale: Keeps compressed historical attribution rather than harmonizing settlement to Joshua.
verses.before: When Jacob went into Egypt, and your ancestors cried out to the LORD, the LORD sent Moses and Aaron, who brought your ancestors out of Egypt and made them dwell in this place.
verses.after: After Jacob went to Egypt, your ancestors cried out to the LORD. He sent Moses and Aaron, who brought your ancestors out of Egypt and settled them in this place.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Jacob went into Egypt, and your ancestors cried out to the LORD, the LORD sent Moses and Aaron, who brought your ancestors out of Egypt and made them dwell in this place.

verses.rationale: Preserves sold/hand metaphor and all three oppressors.
verses.before: But they forgot the LORD their God, and he sold them into the hand of Sisera, commander of the army of Hazor, and into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the king of Moab; and they fought against them.
verses.after: But they forgot the LORD their God. He sold them into the hand of Sisera, commander of Hazor’s army, into the Philistines’ hand, and into the hand of Moab’s king. These fought against them.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they forgot the LORD their God, and he sold them into the hand of Sisera, commander of the army of Hazor, and into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the king of Moab; and they fought against them.

verses.rationale: Follows qere plural said and repeated serve contrast.
verses.before: Then they cried out to the LORD and said, ‘We have sinned, because we have forsaken the LORD and have served the Baals and the Ashtoreths. But now deliver us from the hand of our enemies, and we will serve you.’
verses.after: They cried out to the LORD: ‘We have sinned. We abandoned the LORD and served the Baals and Ashtoreths. Now rescue us from our enemies’ hand, and we will serve you.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they cried out to the LORD and said, ‘We have sinned, because we have forsaken the LORD and have served the Baals and the Ashtoreths. But now deliver us from the hand of our enemies, and we will serve you.’

verses.rationale: Retains pinned Bedan and Samuel rather than replacing with Barak or Samson.
verses.before: And the LORD sent Jerubbaal and Bedan and Jephthah and Samuel, and delivered you from the hand of your enemies all around, and you lived in safety.
verses.after: The LORD sent Jerubbaal, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel. He rescued you from the enemies around you, and you lived securely.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD sent Jerubbaal and Bedan and Jephthah and Samuel, and delivered you from the hand of your enemies all around, and you lived in safety.

verses.rationale: Preserves Samuel’s causal account without rewriting earlier chronology.
verses.before: But when you saw that Nahash king of the Ammonites came against you, you said to me, ‘No, but a king will reign over us,’ though the LORD your God was your king.
verses.after: Yet when you saw Nahash king of the Ammonites coming against you, you told me, ‘No! A king must reign over us,’ although the LORD your God was your king.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when you saw that Nahash king of the Ammonites came against you, you said to me, ‘No, but a king shall reign over us,’ though the LORD your God was your king.

verses.rationale: Keeps people’s choice and LORD’s grant together.
verses.before: And now, see the king whom you have chosen, for whom you have asked. See, the LORD has set a king over you.
verses.after: Now here is the king you chose, the one you asked for. The LORD has given you a king.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, see the king whom you have chosen, for whom you have asked. See, the LORD has set a king over you.

verses.rationale: Keeps conditional obedience and shared king/people duty without added prosperity promise.
verses.before: If you will fear the LORD and serve him and listen to his voice and not rebel against the command of the LORD, and if both you and the king who reigns over you will follow the LORD your God, it will be well.
verses.after: If you fear the LORD, serve him, listen to his voice, and do not rebel against his command, then both you and the king who reigns over you will be following the LORD your God.
verses.tsw_comparator: If you will fear the LORD and serve him and listen to his voice and not rebel against the command of the LORD, and if both you and the king who reigns over you will follow the LORD your God, it will be well.

verses.rationale: Contextual as with ancestors for pinned and against ancestors, disclosed in note.
verses.before: But if you will not listen to the voice of the LORD, but rebel against the command of the LORD, then the hand of the LORD will be against you and against your king.
verses.after: But if you do not listen to the LORD’s voice and rebel against his command, his hand will be against you as it was against your ancestors.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if you will not listen to the voice of the LORD, but rebel against the command of the LORD, then the hand of the LORD will be against you and against your king.

verses.rationale: Retains stand/watch and visible sign.
verses.before: Now therefore stand still and see this great thing that the LORD will do before your eyes.
verses.after: Now stand and watch this great thing the LORD is about to do before your eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now therefore stand still and see this great thing that the LORD will do before your eyes.

verses.rationale: Preserves harvest timing and stated purpose of sign.
verses.before: Is it not the wheat harvest today? I will call to the LORD, and he will give thunder and rain; and you will know and see that your evil is great, which you have done in the sight of the LORD by asking for yourselves a king.”
verses.after: Is it not wheat harvest today? I will call to the LORD, and he will send thunder and rain. Then you will see and know how great an evil you have done in the LORD’s sight by asking for a king.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Is it not the wheat harvest today? I will call to the LORD, and he will give thunder and rain; and you shall know and see that your evil is great, which you have done in the sight of the LORD by asking for yourselves a king.”

verses.rationale: Keeps same-day answer and fear of both figures.
verses.before: So Samuel called to the LORD, and the LORD gave thunder and rain that day; and all the people greatly feared the LORD and Samuel.
verses.after: Samuel called to the LORD, and the LORD sent thunder and rain that day. All the people stood in great fear of the LORD and Samuel.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Samuel called to the LORD, and the LORD gave thunder and rain that day; and all the people greatly feared the LORD and Samuel.

verses.rationale: Retains your God and plea against death.
verses.before: Then all the people said to Samuel, “Pray for your servants to the LORD your God, so that we may not die; for we have added to all our sins this evil, to ask for ourselves a king.”
verses.after: They all said to Samuel, “Pray to the LORD your God for your servants, so we do not die. We have added to all our sins this evil of asking for a king.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then all the people said to Samuel, “Pray for your servants to the LORD your God, so that we may not die; for we have added to all our sins this evil, to ask for ourselves a king.”

verses.rationale: Keeps reassurance and acknowledged wrongdoing together.
verses.before: Samuel said to the people, “Do not fear. You have done all this evil; yet do not turn aside from following the LORD, but serve the LORD with all your heart.
verses.after: Samuel said, “Do not be afraid. You have done all this evil, but do not turn away from following the LORD. Serve him with all your heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel said to the people, “Do not fear. You have done all this evil; yet do not turn aside from following the LORD, but serve the LORD with all your heart.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated tohu without naming only idols in main text.
verses.before: And do not turn aside after empty things that cannot profit or deliver, for they are empty.
verses.after: Do not turn aside to follow empty things that cannot help or rescue you. They are emptiness.
verses.tsw_comparator: And do not turn aside after empty things that cannot profit or deliver, for they are empty.

verses.rationale: Retains name rationale and people repetition.
verses.before: For the LORD will not abandon his people, for his great name’s sake, because the LORD was pleased to make you a people for himself.
verses.after: For the sake of his great name, the LORD will not abandon his people. He was pleased to make you his own people.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the LORD will not abandon his people, for his great name’s sake, because the LORD was pleased to make you a people for himself.

verses.rationale: Keeps continued intercession and teaching despite political transition.
verses.before: Moreover, far be it from me that I should sin against the LORD by ceasing to pray for you; and I will instruct you in the good and right way.
verses.after: As for me, far be it from me to sin against the LORD by ceasing to pray for you. I will teach you the good and upright way.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moreover, far be it from me that I should sin against the LORD by ceasing to pray for you; and I will instruct you in the good and right way.

verses.rationale: Retains wholehearted fidelity grounded in past acts.
verses.before: Only fear the LORD and serve him faithfully with all your heart, for consider what great things he has done for you.
verses.after: Only fear the LORD and serve him faithfully with all your heart. Consider the great things he has done for you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Only fear the LORD and serve him faithfully with all your heart, for consider what great things he has done for you.

verses.rationale: Keeps shared consequence and sweeping image.
verses.before: But if you still do evil, both you and your king will be swept away.”
verses.after: But if you persist in doing evil, both you and your king will be swept away.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But if you still do evil, both you and your king will be swept away.”

verses.rationale: Marks damaged regnal formula rather than inventing age or reign length; exact pinned one-year/two-years wording recorded in note.
verses.before: Saul was ... years old when he became king, and he reigned ... and two years over Israel.
verses.after: Saul was … years old when he became king, and he reigned over Israel for … and two years.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul was ... years old when he became king, and he reigned ... and two years over Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserves allocation totaling three thousand and distinct locations.
verses.before: Saul chose for himself three thousand men from Israel. Two thousand were with Saul at Michmash and in the hill country of Bethel, and one thousand were with Jonathan at Gibeah of Benjamin. The rest of the people he sent away, each man to his tent.
verses.after: Saul chose three thousand men from Israel. Two thousand stayed with him at Michmash and in the hill country of Bethel, and a thousand were with Jonathan at Gibeah of Benjamin. He sent the rest home to their tents.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul chose for himself three thousand men from Israel. Two thousand were with Saul at Michmash and in the hill country of Bethel, and one thousand were with Jonathan at Gibeah of Benjamin. The rest of the people he sent away, each man to his tent.

verses.rationale: Keeps Jonathan as attacker and Saul as herald; notes garrison/official ambiguity.
verses.before: Jonathan struck the Philistine garrison that was at Geba, and the Philistines heard of it. Saul blew the ram’s horn throughout the land, saying, “Let the Hebrews hear!”
verses.after: Jonathan struck the Philistine garrison at Geba, and the Philistines heard about it. Saul sounded the ram’s horn throughout the land: “Let the Hebrews hear!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Jonathan struck the Philistine garrison that was at Geba, and the Philistines heard of it. Saul blew the ram’s horn throughout the land, saying, “Let the Hebrews hear!”

verses.rationale: Preserves report crediting Saul and stench metaphor rather than harmonizing attacker.
verses.before: All Israel heard it said, “Saul has struck the garrison of the Philistines, and Israel has also become odious to the Philistines.” So the people were called together after Saul at Gilgal.
verses.after: All Israel heard the report: “Saul has struck the Philistine garrison, and Israel has become a stench to the Philistines.” The people were summoned to join Saul at Gilgal.
verses.tsw_comparator: All Israel heard it said, “Saul has struck the garrison of the Philistines, and Israel has also become odious to the Philistines.” So the people were called together after Saul at Gilgal.

verses.rationale: Retains pinned thirty thousand and sand image, flags numerical difficulty.
verses.before: The Philistines gathered to fight with Israel: thirty thousand chariots, six thousand horsemen, and people as numerous as the sand that is on the seashore. They went up and camped at Michmash, east of Beth-Aven.
verses.after: The Philistines gathered to fight Israel with thirty thousand chariots, six thousand horsemen, and troops as numerous as the sand on the seashore. They came up and camped at Michmash, east of Beth-aven.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Philistines gathered to fight with Israel: thirty thousand chariots, six thousand horsemen, and people as numerous as the sand that is on the seashore. They went up and camped at Michmash, east of Beth-Aven.

verses.rationale: Preserves five hiding places with uncertain tserihim flagged.
verses.before: When the men of Israel saw that they were in distress, for the people were hard pressed, the people hid themselves in caves, holes, rocks, tombs, and cisterns.
verses.after: The Israelites saw that they were in desperate trouble, with their troops hard pressed. They hid in caves, thickets, rocks, cellars, and cisterns.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the men of Israel saw that they were in distress, for the people were hard pressed, the people hid themselves in caves, holes, rocks, tombs, and cisterns.

verses.rationale: Retains crossing, named lands and trembling remnant.
verses.before: Some Hebrews crossed the Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead. But Saul was still at Gilgal, and all the people following him were trembling.
verses.after: Some Hebrews crossed the Jordan into Gad and Gilead. Saul remained at Gilgal, with all his followers trembling.
verses.tsw_comparator: Some Hebrews crossed the Jordan to the land of Gad and Gilead. But Saul was still at Gilgal, and all the people following him were trembling.

verses.rationale: Preserves seven days and nonarrival without inventing lateness explanation.
verses.before: He waited seven days, according to the appointed time Samuel had set, but Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and the people were scattering from him.
verses.after: He waited seven days, until the time Samuel had set. But Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and the troops were scattering away from Saul.
verses.tsw_comparator: He waited seven days, according to the appointed time Samuel had set, but Samuel did not come to Gilgal, and the people were scattering from him.

verses.rationale: Keeps both requested offerings but only burnt offering performed here.
verses.before: Saul said, “Bring near to me the burnt offering and the offerings of well-being.” And he offered the burnt offering.
verses.after: Saul said, “Bring me the burnt offering and the sacrifices of well-being.” Then he offered the burnt offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul said, “Bring near to me the burnt offering and the offerings of well-being.” And he offered the burnt offering.

verses.rationale: Preserves immediately-after timing and blessing greeting.
verses.before: And it happened as he finished offering the burnt offering that, look, Samuel came. Saul went out to meet him and bless him.
verses.after: Just as he finished offering it, Samuel arrived. Saul went out to meet him and greet him with a blessing.
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened as he finished offering the burnt offering that, behold, Samuel came. Saul went out to meet him and bless him.

verses.rationale: Keeps three stated pressures in Saul’s defense.
verses.before: Samuel said, “What have you done?” Saul said, “Because I saw that the people were scattering from me, and you did not come within the appointed days, and the Philistines were gathering at Michmash,
verses.after: Samuel asked, “What have you done?” Saul replied, “I saw the troops scattering away from me, you had not come at the appointed time, and the Philistines were gathering at Michmash.
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel said, “What have you done?” Saul said, “Because I saw that the people were scattering from me, and you did not come within the appointed days, and the Philistines were gathering at Michmash,

verses.rationale: Preserves claimed compulsion as Saul’s account.
verses.before: I said, ‘Now the Philistines will come down against me at Gilgal, and I have not sought the favor of the LORD.’ So I forced myself and offered the burnt offering.”
verses.after: I thought, ‘Now the Philistines will come down against me at Gilgal, and I have not sought the LORD’s favor.’ So I forced myself to offer the burnt offering.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I said, ‘Now the Philistines will come down against me at Gilgal, and I have not sought the favor of the LORD.’ So I forced myself and offered the burnt offering.”

verses.rationale: Keeps disobedience and counterfactual enduring kingdom.
verses.before: Samuel said to Saul, “You have acted foolishly. You have not kept the commandment of the LORD your God that he commanded you. For now the LORD would have established your kingdom over Israel forever.
verses.after: Samuel told Saul, “You have acted foolishly. You have not kept the command the LORD your God gave you. The LORD would have established your kingdom over Israel forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel said to Saul, “You have acted foolishly. You have not kept the commandment of the LORD your God that he commanded you. For now the LORD would have established your kingdom over Israel forever.

verses.rationale: Retains heart expression without converting to claim of moral perfection or naming David yet.
verses.before: But now your kingdom will not continue. The LORD has sought for himself a man according to his heart, and the LORD has appointed him as ruler over his people, because you did not keep what the LORD commanded you.”
verses.after: But now your kingdom will not endure. The LORD has sought a man after his own heart and appointed him leader over his people, because you did not keep the LORD’s command.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But now your kingdom shall not continue. The LORD has sought for himself a man according to his heart, and the LORD has appointed him as ruler over his people, because you did not keep what the LORD commanded you.”

verses.rationale: Keeps pinned Samuel movement and approximate remaining force.
verses.before: Samuel arose and went up from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin. Saul counted the people who were found with him, about six hundred men.
verses.after: Samuel got up and went from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin. Saul counted the men still with him: about six hundred.
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel arose and went up from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin. Saul counted the people who were found with him, about six hundred men.

verses.rationale: Preserves Geba distinct from preceding Gibeah.
verses.before: Saul and Jonathan his son and the people found with them were staying at Geba of Benjamin, while the Philistines camped at Michmash.
verses.after: Saul, his son Jonathan, and the men with them were staying at Geba of Benjamin. The Philistines camped at Michmash.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul and Jonathan his son and the people found with them were staying at Geba of Benjamin, while the Philistines camped at Michmash.

verses.rationale: Keeps three groups and first direction.
verses.before: Raiders came out from the camp of the Philistines in three companies. One company turned toward the way of Ophrah, toward the land of Shual;
verses.after: Three raiding companies came out of the Philistine camp. One headed toward Ophrah in the land of Shual.
verses.tsw_comparator: Raiders came out from the camp of the Philistines in three companies. One company turned toward the way of Ophrah, toward the land of Shual;

verses.rationale: Preserves both remaining routes and wilderness orientation.
verses.before: another company turned toward the way of Beth-Horon; and another company turned toward the way of the border overlooking the Valley of Zeboim toward the wilderness.
verses.after: Another headed toward Beth-horon, and the third toward the border overlooking the Valley of Zeboim, toward the wilderness.
verses.tsw_comparator: another company turned toward the way of Beth-Horon; and another company turned toward the way of the border overlooking the Valley of Zeboim toward the wilderness.

verses.rationale: Keeps imposed weapons restriction and quoted outsider designation.
verses.before: Now no blacksmith was found throughout all the land of Israel, for the Philistines said, “Lest the Hebrews make sword or spear.”
verses.after: No smith could be found anywhere in Israel, for the Philistines had said, “The Hebrews must not make swords or spears.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now no blacksmith was found throughout all the land of Israel, for the Philistines said, “Lest the Hebrews make sword or spear.”

verses.rationale: Differentiates uncertain agricultural tool list without pretending exact identifications secure.
verses.before: So all Israel went down to the Philistines, each to sharpen his plowshare, mattock, axe, and sickle.
verses.after: So all Israel had to go down to the Philistines to sharpen their plowshares, mattocks, axes, and hoes.
verses.tsw_comparator: So all Israel went down to the Philistines, each to sharpen his plowshare, mattock, axe, and sickle.

verses.rationale: Retains ancient price unit and difficult tool wording with note rather than invented precise modern fee.
verses.before: The charge was a pim for the plowshares and mattocks and one-third of a shekel for sharpening the axes and setting the goads.
verses.after: The sharpening charge was a pim for plowshares and mattocks, for three-pronged forks and axes, and for setting the goads.
verses.tsw_comparator: The charge was a pim for the plowshares and mattocks and one-third of a shekel for sharpening the axes and setting the goads.

verses.rationale: Preserves stated contrast without adding weapons to unnamed soldiers.
verses.before: So it happened on the day of battle that neither sword nor spear was found in the hand of any of the people who were with Saul and Jonathan, but they were found with Saul and Jonathan his son.
verses.after: On the day of battle, none of the troops with Saul and Jonathan had a sword or spear. Only Saul and his son Jonathan had them.
verses.tsw_comparator: So it happened on the day of battle that neither sword nor spear was found in the hand of any of the people who were with Saul and Jonathan, but they were found with Saul and Jonathan his son.

verses.rationale: Keeps transition into Jonathan’s next action.
verses.before: And a garrison of the Philistines went out to the pass of Michmash.
verses.after: A Philistine outpost moved out to the pass at Michmash.
verses.tsw_comparator: And a garrison of the Philistines went out to the pass of Michmash.

verses.rationale: Keeps private initiative and armor-bearer’s role.
verses.before: One day Jonathan son of Saul said to the young man carrying his armor, “Come, let us cross over to the Philistine garrison that is on the other side.” But he did not tell his father.
verses.after: One day Jonathan son of Saul said to the young man carrying his armor, “Come, let us cross over to the Philistine outpost on the other side.” He did not tell his father.
verses.tsw_comparator: One day Jonathan son of Saul said to the young man carrying his armor, “Come, let us cross over to the Philistine garrison that is on the other side.” But he did not tell his father.

verses.rationale: Retains tree, location and approximate force.
verses.before: Saul was staying at the edge of Gibeah under the pomegranate tree that is in Migron, and the people who were with him were about six hundred men.
verses.after: Saul was staying on the outskirts of Gibeah, under the pomegranate tree at Migron. About six hundred men were with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul was staying at the edge of Gibeah under the pomegranate tree that is in Migron, and the people who were with him were about six hundred men.

verses.rationale: Preserves genealogy while separating priest’s presence from ignorance of departure.
verses.before: Ahijah son of Ahitub, brother of Ichabod, son of Phinehas, son of Eli, priest of the LORD at Shiloh, was wearing an ephod. The people did not know that Jonathan had gone.
verses.after: Ahijah was there wearing an ephod. He was the son of Ahitub, Ichabod’s brother, son of Phinehas, son of Eli, the LORD’s priest at Shiloh. The troops did not know Jonathan had gone.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ahijah son of Ahitub, brother of Ichabod, son of Phinehas, son of Eli, priest of the LORD at Shiloh, was wearing an ephod. The people did not know that Jonathan had gone.

verses.rationale: Keeps tooth image and both crag names.
verses.before: Between the passes by which Jonathan sought to cross over to the Philistine garrison, there was a rocky crag on one side and a rocky crag on the other side. The name of one was Bozez, and the name of the other Seneh.
verses.after: On either side of the pass Jonathan intended to cross to reach the Philistine outpost, a tooth of rock rose up. One was named Bozez and the other Seneh.
verses.tsw_comparator: Between the passes by which Jonathan sought to cross over to the Philistine garrison, there was a rocky crag on one side and a rocky crag on the other side. The name of one was Bozez, and the name of the other Seneh.

verses.rationale: Preserves orientations and distinct sites.
verses.before: One crag rose on the north opposite Michmash, and the other on the south opposite Geba.
verses.after: One tooth rose on the north, facing Michmash; the other stood on the south, facing Geba.
verses.tsw_comparator: One crag rose on the north opposite Michmash, and the other on the south opposite Geba.

verses.rationale: Retains uncircumcised, tentative perhaps and many/few contrast.
verses.before: Jonathan said to the young man carrying his armor, “Come, let us cross over to the garrison of these uncircumcised. Perhaps the LORD will act for us, for nothing restrains the LORD from saving by many or by few.”
verses.after: Jonathan said to his armor-bearer, “Come, let us cross over to the outpost of these uncircumcised men. Perhaps the LORD will act for us. Nothing prevents the LORD from saving, whether by many or by few.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Jonathan said to the young man carrying his armor, “Come, let us cross over to the garrison of these uncircumcised. Perhaps the LORD will act for us, for nothing restrains the LORD from saving by many or by few.”

verses.rationale: Keeps doubled heart solidarity in natural speech.
verses.before: His armor-bearer said to him, “Do all that is in your heart. Turn where you wish. Look, I am with you according to your heart.”
verses.after: His armor-bearer answered, “Do all that is in your heart. Go ahead. I am with you, heart and all.”
verses.tsw_comparator: His armor-bearer said to him, “Do all that is in your heart. Turn where you wish. Look, I am with you according to your heart.”

verses.rationale: Preserves plan’s deliberate exposure.
verses.before: Jonathan said, “Look, we will cross over to the men and reveal ourselves to them.
verses.after: Jonathan said, “We will cross over to the men and let them see us.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jonathan said, “Look, we will cross over to the men and reveal ourselves to them.

verses.rationale: Keeps first conditional response and restraint.
verses.before: If they say to us, ‘Wait until we come to you,’ then we will stand in our place and not go up to them.
verses.after: If they say, ‘Stay there until we reach you,’ we will stay where we are and not go up to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: If they say to us, ‘Wait until we come to you,’ then we will stand in our place and not go up to them.

verses.rationale: Preserves second condition and interpreted sign.
verses.before: But if they say, ‘Come up to us,’ then we will go up, for the LORD has given them into our hand. This will be the sign for us.”
verses.after: But if they say, ‘Come up to us,’ we will go up, because the LORD has given them into our hand. That will be our sign.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But if they say, ‘Come up to us,’ then we will go up, for the LORD has given them into our hand. This shall be the sign for us.”

verses.rationale: Retains mocking enemy observation and holes.
verses.before: The two of them revealed themselves to the Philistine garrison. The Philistines said, “Look, Hebrews are coming out from the holes where they hid themselves.”
verses.after: The two of them showed themselves to the Philistine outpost. The Philistines said, “Look! Hebrews are coming out of the holes where they have been hiding.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The two of them revealed themselves to the Philistine garrison. The Philistines said, “Look, Hebrews are coming out from the holes where they hid themselves.”

verses.rationale: Keeps taunt and Israel-wide claim rather than only personal victory.
verses.before: The men of the garrison answered Jonathan and his armor-bearer and said, “Come up to us, and we will make something known to you.” Jonathan said to his armor-bearer, “Come up after me, for the LORD has given them into the hand of Israel.”
verses.after: The men of the outpost called to Jonathan and his armor-bearer, “Come up here. We will teach you something!” Jonathan told his armor-bearer, “Come up after me. The LORD has given them into Israel’s hand.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The men of the garrison answered Jonathan and his armor-bearer and said, “Come up to us, and we will make something known to you.” Jonathan said to his armor-bearer, “Come up after me, for the LORD has given them into the hand of Israel.”

verses.rationale: Preserves physical climb and second man’s lethal role.
verses.before: Jonathan climbed up on his hands and his feet, and his armor-bearer after him. They fell before Jonathan, and his armor-bearer put them to death after him.
verses.after: Jonathan climbed up on his hands and feet, his armor-bearer behind him. The Philistines fell before Jonathan, and his armor-bearer followed, killing them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jonathan climbed up on his hands and his feet, and his armor-bearer after him. They fell before Jonathan, and his armor-bearer put them to death after him.

verses.rationale: Retains obscure agricultural area description without asserting modern acreage.
verses.before: That first slaughter that Jonathan and his armor-bearer struck was about twenty men within about half a furrow in an acre of field.
verses.after: In that first attack, Jonathan and his armor-bearer struck down about twenty men within roughly half a furrow of a field a pair of oxen could plow.
verses.tsw_comparator: That first slaughter that Jonathan and his armor-bearer struck was about twenty men within about half a furrow in an acre of field.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine/superlative ambiguity in note and earth movement.
verses.before: Then there was trembling in the camp, in the field, and among all the people. The garrison and the raiders also trembled. The earth quaked, and it became a trembling from God.
verses.after: Terror spread through the camp, the field, and all the troops. The outpost and the raiders trembled too. The earth shook. It was a terror from God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then there was trembling in the camp, in the field, and among all the people. The garrison and the raiders also trembled. The earth quaked, and it became a trembling from God.

verses.rationale: Keeps visual dissolution and difficult movement wording.
verses.before: Saul’s watchmen in Gibeah of Benjamin looked, and look, the multitude was melting away and going here and there.
verses.after: Saul’s lookouts at Gibeah of Benjamin saw the enemy mass melting away, surging here and there.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul’s watchmen in Gibeah of Benjamin looked, and behold, the multitude was melting away and going here and there.

verses.rationale: Preserves discovery through muster.
verses.before: Saul said to the people who were with him, “Please count and see who has gone from us.” They counted, and look, Jonathan and his armor-bearer were not there.
verses.after: Saul told the men with him, “Take a count and see who has left us.” They counted and found Jonathan and his armor-bearer missing.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul said to the people who were with him, “Please count and see who has gone from us.” They counted, and behold, Jonathan and his armor-bearer were not there.

verses.rationale: Keeps pinned ark despite ephod context, variant noted.
verses.before: Saul said to Ahijah, “Bring near the ark of God.” For the ark of God was at that time with the children of Israel.
verses.after: Saul told Ahijah, “Bring the ark of God here.” The ark of God was with the Israelites that day.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul said to Ahijah, “Bring near the ark of God.” For the ark of God was at that time with the children of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains abrupt ending of inquiry without explaining ritual beyond source.
verses.before: And it happened while Saul was speaking to the priest that the tumult in the camp of the Philistines kept increasing. So Saul said to the priest, “Withdraw your hand.”
verses.after: While Saul was speaking to the priest, the uproar in the Philistine camp kept growing. Saul said to the priest, “Withdraw your hand.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And it happened while Saul was speaking to the priest that the tumult in the camp of the Philistines kept increasing. So Saul said to the priest, “Withdraw your hand.”

verses.rationale: Clarifies enemy referent and mutual sword violence.
verses.before: Saul and all the people who were with him were called together and came to the battle. And look, every Philistine’s sword was against his companion, a very great confusion.
verses.after: Saul and all the men with him rallied and went into battle. There they found the Philistines turning their swords on one another in overwhelming confusion.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul and all the people who were with him were called together and came to the battle. And behold, every Philistine’s sword was against his companion, a very great confusion.

verses.rationale: Preserves changed allegiance without deciding status as slaves or mercenaries.
verses.before: Now the Hebrews who had been with the Philistines formerly, who had gone up with them into the camp all around, even they turned to be with Israel who were with Saul and Jonathan.
verses.after: The Hebrews who had previously been with the Philistines and had gone up with them into the camp now joined the Israelites with Saul and Jonathan.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the Hebrews who had been with the Philistines formerly, who had gone up with them into the camp all around, even they turned to be with Israel who were with Saul and Jonathan.

verses.rationale: Keeps emergence of hidden troops.
