verses.after: All the Israelites hiding in the hill country of Ephraim heard that the Philistines were fleeing. They too joined the pursuit in battle.
verses.tsw_comparator: Also all the men of Israel who had hidden themselves in the hill country of Ephraim heard that the Philistines were fleeing, and they too pursued them closely in the battle.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine credit and geographic advance.
verses.before: So the LORD saved Israel that day, and the battle passed beyond Beth-Aven.
verses.after: That day the LORD saved Israel, and the battle moved beyond Beth-aven.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the LORD saved Israel that day, and the battle passed beyond Beth-Aven.

verses.rationale: Retains personal revenge and coercive fasting oath.
verses.before: Now the men of Israel were hard pressed that day, for Saul had put the people under an oath, saying, “Cursed is the man who eats food before evening and before I am avenged on my enemies.” So none of the people tasted food.
verses.after: The men of Israel were hard pressed that day because Saul had put them under an oath: “Cursed is anyone who eats before evening, before I have taken vengeance on my enemies.” So none of the troops tasted food.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the men of Israel were hard pressed that day, for Saul had put the people under an oath, saying, “Cursed is the man who eats food before evening and before I am avenged on my enemies.” So none of the people tasted food.

verses.rationale: Contextual people for all the land, retains accessible honey.
verses.before: All the people of the land came into the forest, and there was honey upon the ground.
verses.after: All the people entered the forest, where honey lay on the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the people of the land came into the forest, and there was honey upon the ground.

verses.rationale: Keeps embodied restraint and fear.
verses.before: When the people came into the forest, look, honey was dripping, but no one put his hand to his mouth, for the people feared the oath.
verses.after: As they entered, they saw honey flowing, but no one put a hand to his mouth. They feared the oath.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the people came into the forest, behold, honey was dripping, but no one put his hand to his mouth, for the people feared the oath.

verses.rationale: Follows qere brightened and preserves ignorance before action.
verses.before: Yet Jonathan had not heard when his father put the people under oath. He stretched out the end of the staff that was in his hand, dipped it in the honeycomb, and returned his hand to his mouth, and his eyes became bright.
verses.after: Jonathan had not heard his father put the troops under oath. He reached out the end of his staff, dipped it into the honeycomb, and brought his hand to his mouth. His eyes brightened.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Jonathan had not heard when his father put the people under oath. He stretched out the end of the staff that was in his hand, dipped it in the honeycomb, and returned his hand to his mouth, and his eyes became bright.

verses.rationale: Keeps quoted oath and narrator’s exhaustion statement distinct.
verses.before: Then one man from the people answered and said, “Your father strictly put the people under oath, saying, ‘Cursed is the man who eats food today.’” And the people were faint.
verses.after: One of the men told him, “Your father solemnly bound the troops with an oath: ‘Cursed is anyone who eats today.’” The troops were exhausted.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then one man from the people answered and said, “Your father strictly put the people under oath, saying, ‘Cursed is the man who eats food today.’” And the people were faint.

verses.rationale: Retains trouble-on-land idiom and visible counterexample.
verses.before: Jonathan said, “My father has troubled the land. See, please, how my eyes have become bright because I tasted a little of this honey.
verses.after: Jonathan said, “My father has brought trouble on the land. Look how my eyes have brightened after tasting a little of this honey.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jonathan said, “My father has troubled the land. See, please, how my eyes have become bright because I tasted a little of this honey.

verses.rationale: Preserves counterfactual military critique and rhetorical final question.
verses.before: How much more if the people had freely eaten today from the spoil of their enemies that they found! For now the slaughter among the Philistines has not been great.”
verses.after: How much better if the troops had eaten freely today from the enemy plunder they found! Would the slaughter among the Philistines not have been greater?”
verses.tsw_comparator: How much more if the people had freely eaten today from the spoil of their enemies that they found! For now the slaughter among the Philistines has not been great.”

verses.rationale: Keeps pursuit span and repeated exhaustion.
verses.before: They struck the Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon, and the people became very faint.
verses.after: That day they struck the Philistines from Michmash to Aijalon. The troops were utterly exhausted.
verses.tsw_comparator: They struck the Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon, and the people became very faint.

verses.rationale: Follows qere pounced and preserves three animal groups and blood violation.
verses.before: The people rushed upon the spoil, took sheep, cattle, and calves, slaughtered them on the ground, and the people ate them with the blood.
verses.after: They pounced on the plunder, took sheep, cattle, and calves, and slaughtered them on the ground. They ate the meat with the blood.
verses.tsw_comparator: The people rushed upon the spoil, took sheep, cattle, and calves, slaughtered them on the ground, and the people ate them with the blood.

verses.rationale: Keeps report, judgment and concrete remedy.
verses.before: They told Saul, saying, “Look, the people are sinning against the LORD by eating with the blood.” He said, “You have acted unfaithfully. Roll a great stone to me today.”
verses.after: Saul was told, “The troops are sinning against the LORD by eating with the blood.” He said, “You have acted faithlessly. Roll a large stone over to me now.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They told Saul, saying, “Look, the people are sinning against the LORD by eating with the blood.” He said, “You have acted unfaithfully. Roll a great stone to me today.”

verses.rationale: Preserves distributed instruction and night compliance.
verses.before: Saul said, “Scatter yourselves among the people and say to them, ‘Bring near to me each his ox and each his sheep, slaughter them here and eat. Do not sin against the LORD by eating with the blood.’” So all the people brought near each his ox in his hand that night and slaughtered them there.
verses.after: Then he said, “Spread out among the troops and tell them: ‘Each of you bring me your ox or sheep. Slaughter it here and eat. Do not sin against the LORD by eating with the blood.’” That night everyone brought his ox and slaughtered it there.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul said, “Scatter yourselves among the people and say to them, ‘Bring near to me each his ox and each his sheep, slaughter them here and eat. Do not sin against the LORD by eating with the blood.’” So all the people brought near each his ox in his hand that night and slaughtered them there.

verses.rationale: Uses first-altar reading of began to build without importing earlier altar.
verses.before: Saul built an altar to the LORD; it was the first altar he built to the LORD.
verses.after: Saul built an altar to the LORD. This was the first altar he built to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul built an altar to the LORD; it was the first altar he built to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps exterminating plan and priest’s interruption explicit.
verses.before: Saul said, “Let us go down after the Philistines by night and plunder them until the morning light, and let us not leave a man among them.” They said, “Do whatever is good in your eyes.” But the priest said, “Let us draw near here to God.”
verses.after: Saul said, “Let us go down after the Philistines tonight and plunder them until morning light. Let us leave none of them alive.” The men answered, “Do whatever seems good to you.” But the priest said, “Let us approach God here.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul said, “Let us go down after the Philistines by night and plunder them until the morning light, and let us not leave a man among them.” They said, “Do whatever is good in your eyes.” But the priest said, “Let us draw near here to God.”

verses.rationale: Retains two questions and divine silence.
verses.before: Saul inquired of God, “Will I go down after the Philistines? Will you give them into the hand of Israel?” But he did not answer him that day.
verses.after: Saul inquired of God, “Shall I go down after the Philistines? Will you give them into Israel’s hand?” But God did not answer him that day.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul inquired of God, “Shall I go down after the Philistines? Will you give them into the hand of Israel?” But he did not answer him that day.

verses.rationale: Retains leaders’ inquiry and Saul’s inference of sin.
verses.before: Saul said, “Come near here, all the chiefs of the people, and know and see how this sin happened today.
verses.after: Saul said, “Come here, all you leaders of the troops. Find out what sin has been committed today.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul said, “Come near here, all the chiefs of the people, and know and see how this sin happened today.

verses.rationale: Keeps second rash oath and people’s silence.
verses.before: For as the LORD lives, who saves Israel, even if it is in Jonathan my son, he will surely die.” But there was no one among all the people who answered him.
verses.after: As the LORD lives, who saves Israel, even if the guilt lies with my son Jonathan, he must die.” Not one of the troops answered him.
verses.tsw_comparator: For as the LORD lives, who saves Israel, even if it is in Jonathan my son, he shall surely die.” But there was no one among all the people who answered him.

verses.rationale: Preserves two groups and repeated acquiescence.
verses.before: He said to all Israel, “You will be on one side, and I and Jonathan my son will be on the other side.” The people said to Saul, “Do what is good in your eyes.”
verses.after: He told all Israel, “You stand on one side; my son Jonathan and I will stand on the other.” The people replied, “Do whatever seems good to you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to all Israel, “You shall be on one side, and I and Jonathan my son will be on the other side.” The people said to Saul, “Do what is good in your eyes.”

verses.rationale: Uses short pinned habah tamim without silently importing longer Urim/Thummim witness.
verses.before: Saul said to the LORD, the God of Israel, “Give a perfect lot.” And Jonathan and Saul were taken, but the people went free.
verses.after: Saul said to the LORD, the God of Israel, “Give a true answer.” Jonathan and Saul were selected, and the people were cleared.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul said to the LORD, the God of Israel, “Give a perfect lot.” And Jonathan and Saul were taken, but the people went free.

verses.rationale: Makes casting explicit from hippilu while retaining passive selection.
verses.before: Saul said, “Cast between me and Jonathan my son.” And Jonathan was taken.
verses.after: Saul said, “Cast the lot between me and my son Jonathan.” Jonathan was selected.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul said, “Cast between me and Jonathan my son.” And Jonathan was taken.

verses.rationale: Preserves terse death statement rather than silently turning it into a question.
verses.before: Then Saul said to Jonathan, “Tell me what you have done.” Jonathan told him and said, “I merely tasted a little honey with the end of the staff that was in my hand. Look, I will die.”
verses.after: Saul asked Jonathan, “Tell me what you have done.” Jonathan told him, “I only tasted a little honey with the end of the staff in my hand. Here I am, to die.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Saul said to Jonathan, “Tell me what you have done.” Jonathan told him and said, “I merely tasted a little honey with the end of the staff that was in my hand. Look, I will die.”

verses.rationale: Keeps unspecified oath and explicit death sentence.
verses.before: Saul said, “Thus may God do and more also, for you will surely die, Jonathan.”
verses.after: Saul said, “May God do this, and more besides! You will certainly die, Jonathan.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul said, “Thus may God do and more also, for you shall surely die, Jonathan.”

verses.rationale: Retains counter-oath, hair image and redemption without inventing payment.
verses.before: But the people said to Saul, “Will Jonathan die, who has worked this great salvation in Israel? Far be it! As the LORD lives, not one hair of his head will fall to the ground, for with God he has worked this day.” So the people ransomed Jonathan, and he did not die.
verses.after: But the people said to Saul, “Must Jonathan die, the one who brought this great deliverance to Israel? Far be it! As the LORD lives, not a hair of his head will fall to the ground, for he has worked with God today.” So the people redeemed Jonathan, and he did not die.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the people said to Saul, “Shall Jonathan die, who has worked this great salvation in Israel? Far be it! As the LORD lives, not one hair of his head shall fall to the ground, for with God he has worked this day.” So the people ransomed Jonathan, and he did not die.

verses.rationale: Keeps pursuit’s end and enemy departure.
verses.before: Then Saul went up from pursuing the Philistines, and the Philistines went to their own place.
verses.after: Saul broke off the pursuit of the Philistines, and they returned to their own place.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Saul went up from pursuing the Philistines, and the Philistines went to their own place.

verses.rationale: Preserves pinned yarshia judgment sense with difficult victory alternative noted.
verses.before: When Saul had taken the kingship over Israel, he fought against all his enemies around: against Moab, the children of Ammon, Edom, the kings of Zobah, and the Philistines. Wherever he turned, he inflicted punishment.
verses.after: Saul secured the kingship over Israel and fought all his enemies on every side: Moab, the Ammonites, Edom, the kings of Zobah, and the Philistines. Wherever he turned, he inflicted punishment.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Saul had taken the kingship over Israel, he fought against all his enemies around: against Moab, the children of Ammon, Edom, the kings of Zobah, and the Philistines. Wherever he turned, he inflicted punishment.

verses.rationale: Keeps valor and rescue in positive reign summary.
verses.before: He acted valiantly and struck Amalek and rescued Israel from the hand of people who plundered them.
verses.after: He acted valiantly, struck Amalek, and rescued Israel from those who plundered it.
verses.tsw_comparator: He acted valiantly and struck Amalek and rescued Israel from the hand of those who plundered them.

verses.rationale: Preserves all names and daughters’ relative ages without harmonizing other son lists.
verses.before: The sons of Saul were Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchi-Shua. The names of his two daughters were these: the name of the firstborn Merab and the name of the younger Michal.
verses.after: Saul’s sons were Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchi-shua. His two daughters were Merab, the older, and Michal, the younger.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sons of Saul were Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchi-Shua. The names of his two daughters were these: the name of the firstborn Merab and the name of the younger Michal.

verses.rationale: Attaches uncle to Ner in light of next verse, flagged relationship choice.
verses.before: The name of Saul’s wife was Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz. The name of the commander of his army was Abner son of Ner, Saul’s uncle.
verses.after: Saul’s wife was Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz. His army commander was Abner, son of Saul’s uncle Ner.
verses.tsw_comparator: The name of Saul’s wife was Ahinoam daughter of Ahimaaz. The name of the commander of his army was Abner son of Ner, Saul’s uncle.

verses.rationale: Reads compressed genealogy as brothers with shared father, retains names and roles.
verses.before: Kish was Saul’s father, and Ner father of Abner was son of Abiel.
verses.after: Kish, Saul’s father, and Ner, Abner’s father, were sons of Abiel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Kish was Saul’s father, and Ner father of Abner was son of Abiel.

verses.rationale: Keeps ongoing war and royal recruitment echoing chapter 8.
verses.before: The war against the Philistines was severe all the days of Saul. Whenever Saul saw any mighty man or any valiant man, he gathered him to himself.
verses.after: Fierce war with the Philistines continued throughout Saul’s days. Whenever he saw a strong man or a capable warrior, he took him into his service.
verses.tsw_comparator: The war against the Philistines was severe all the days of Saul. Whenever Saul saw any mighty man or any valiant man, he gathered him to himself.

verses.rationale: Retains authority of anointing and hearing command.
verses.before: Samuel said to Saul, “The LORD sent me to anoint you king over his people, over Israel. And now listen to the voice of the words of the LORD.
verses.after: Samuel told Saul, “The LORD sent me to anoint you king over his people Israel. Now listen to the LORD’s words.
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel said to Saul, “The LORD sent me to anoint you king over his people, over Israel. And now listen to the voice of the words of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Renders punitive paqad while retaining historical road offense.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: I have attended to what Amalek did to Israel, how he set himself against him on the way when he came up from Egypt.
verses.after: This is what the LORD of Armies says: ‘I will call Amalek to account for what it did to Israel, opposing Israel on the road out of Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: I have attended to what Amalek did to Israel, how he set himself against him on the way when he came up from Egypt.

verses.rationale: Preserves herem terminology and every named human and animal category without softening killing.
verses.before: Now go and strike Amalek and devote to destruction all that belongs to him. Do not spare him, but put to death man and woman, child and nursing infant, ox and sheep, camel and donkey.”
verses.after: Now go and strike Amalek. Devote everything it has to destruction. Do not spare anyone. Put to death men and women, children and nursing infants, cattle and sheep, camels and donkeys.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now go and strike Amalek and devote to destruction all that belongs to him. Do not spare him, but put to death man and woman, child and nursing infant, ox and sheep, camel and donkey.”

verses.rationale: Retains place and separate force counts.
verses.before: Saul summoned the people and mustered them at Telaim: two hundred thousand foot soldiers and ten thousand men of Judah.
verses.after: Saul summoned the troops and mustered them at Telaim: two hundred thousand foot soldiers and ten thousand men of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul summoned the people and mustered them at Telaim: two hundred thousand foot soldiers and ten thousand men of Judah.

verses.rationale: Uses ambush understanding of difficult wayyareb with terrain retained.
verses.before: Saul came to the city of Amalek and lay in wait in the wadi.
verses.after: Saul reached Amalek’s city and set an ambush in the wadi.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul came to the city of Amalek and lay in wait in the wadi.

verses.rationale: Keeps hesed and threatened sweep, differentiating Kenites from targets.
verses.before: Saul said to the Kenites, “Go, turn aside, go down from among the Amalekites, lest I sweep you away with them, for you showed steadfast love to all the children of Israel when they came up from Egypt.” So the Kenites turned aside from the midst of Amalek.
verses.after: He told the Kenites, “Go, leave the Amalekites. Get away from them so I do not sweep you away with them. You showed steadfast love to all the Israelites when they came up from Egypt.” So the Kenites withdrew from among the Amalekites.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul said to the Kenites, “Go, turn aside, go down from among the Amalekites, lest I sweep you away with them, for you showed steadfast love to all the children of Israel when they came up from Egypt.” So the Kenites turned aside from the midst of Amalek.

verses.rationale: Retains named range and Egyptian orientation.
verses.before: Saul struck Amalek from Havilah as far as Shur, which is east of Egypt.
verses.after: Saul struck Amalek from Havilah as far as Shur, east of Egypt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul struck Amalek from Havilah as far as Shur, which is east of Egypt.

verses.rationale: Preserves exception for king and totalizing killing claim as narrated.
verses.before: He captured Agag king of Amalek alive and devoted all the people to destruction with the edge of the sword.
verses.after: He captured Agag king of Amalek alive, but devoted all the people to destruction by the sword.
verses.tsw_comparator: He captured Agag king of Amalek alive and devoted all the people to destruction with the edge of the sword.

verses.rationale: Retains Saul with troops as actors and selective destruction; uncertain animal term noted.
verses.before: Yet Saul and the people spared Agag and the best of the sheep, cattle, second-born animals, lambs, and all that was good, and they were not willing to devote them to destruction. But everything despised and worthless, that they devoted to destruction.
verses.after: Saul and the troops spared Agag and the best sheep, cattle, fattened animals, and lambs—everything good. They refused to devote these to destruction. They destroyed only what was despised and worthless.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Saul and the people spared Agag and the best of the sheep, cattle, second-born animals, lambs, and all that was good, and they were not willing to devote them to destruction. But everything despised and worthless, that they devoted to destruction.

verses.rationale: Keeps prophetic transition.
verses.before: Then the word of the LORD came to Samuel, saying,
verses.after: The LORD’s word came to Samuel:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the word of the LORD came to Samuel, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps divine regret and Samuel’s anger rather than reducing to sadness.
verses.before: “I regret that I made Saul king, for he has turned back from following me and has not established my words.” Samuel became angry, and he cried out to the LORD all night.
verses.after: “I regret making Saul king. He has turned away from following me and has not carried out my words.” Samuel burned with anger and cried out to the LORD all night.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I regret that I made Saul king, for he has turned back from following me and has not established my words.” Samuel became angry, and he cried out to the LORD all night.

verses.rationale: Keeps self-monument and journey reported before meeting.
verses.before: Samuel rose early to meet Saul in the morning, and it was told to Samuel, saying, “Saul came to Carmel, and look, he set up a monument for himself, then turned and passed on and went down to Gilgal.”
verses.after: Samuel rose early to meet Saul. He was told, “Saul went to Carmel and set up a monument for himself. Then he turned and went on down to Gilgal.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel rose early to meet Saul in the morning, and it was told to Samuel, saying, “Saul came to Carmel, and look, he set up a monument for himself, then turned and passed on and went down to Gilgal.”

verses.rationale: Preserves claim contradicting divine assessment.
verses.before: Samuel came to Saul, and Saul said to him, “Blessed are you by the LORD! I have established the word of the LORD.”
verses.after: When Samuel reached him, Saul said, “May the LORD bless you! I have carried out the LORD’s word.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel came to Saul, and Saul said to him, “Blessed are you by the LORD! I have established the word of the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Keeps two sounds and hearing theme exposing claim.
verses.before: Samuel said, “Then what is this sound of sheep in my ears and the sound of cattle that I hear?”
verses.after: Samuel asked, “Then what is this sound of sheep in my ears? What is this sound of cattle I hear?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel said, “Then what is this sound of sheep in my ears and the sound of cattle that I hear?”

verses.rationale: Preserves they/troops/we shifts and your God.
verses.before: Saul said, “They brought them from the Amalekites, for the people spared the best of the sheep and cattle to sacrifice to the LORD your God, and the rest we devoted to destruction.”
verses.after: Saul answered, “They brought them from the Amalekites. The troops spared the best sheep and cattle to sacrifice to the LORD your God. We devoted the rest to destruction.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul said, “They brought them from the Amalekites, for the people spared the best of the sheep and cattle to sacrifice to the LORD your God, and the rest we devoted to destruction.”

verses.rationale: Follows qere singular response and abrupt interruption.
verses.before: Samuel said to Saul, “Stop! And I will tell you what the LORD spoke to me this night.” He said to him, “Speak.”
verses.after: “Stop,” Samuel told Saul. “Let me tell you what the LORD said to me last night.” Saul replied, “Speak.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel said to Saul, “Stop! And I will tell you what the LORD spoke to me this night.” He said to him, “Speak.”

verses.rationale: Keeps self-perception contrast and royal responsibility.
verses.before: Samuel said, “Though you were small in your own eyes, were you not the head of the tribes of Israel? The LORD anointed you king over Israel.
verses.after: Samuel said, “Though you may be small in your own eyes, are you not the head of Israel’s tribes? The LORD anointed you king over Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel said, “Though you were small in your own eyes, were you not the head of the tribes of Israel? The LORD anointed you king over Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains stated sinners category and extermination command as Samuel’s quotation.
verses.before: The LORD sent you on a mission and said, ‘Go and devote to destruction the sinners, Amalek, and fight against them until you have finished them.’
verses.after: The LORD sent you on a mission: ‘Go and devote the sinners, the Amalekites, to destruction. Fight against them until you have wiped them out.’
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD sent you on a mission and said, ‘Go and devote to destruction the sinners, Amalek, and fight against them until you have finished them.’

verses.rationale: Keeps hearing/sight and pounce link to 14:32.
verses.before: Why then did you not listen to the voice of the LORD, but swooped down upon the spoil and did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD?”
verses.after: Why did you not listen to the LORD’s voice? Why did you pounce on the plunder and do what is evil in his sight?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Why then did you not listen to the voice of the LORD, but swooped down upon the spoil and did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD?”

verses.rationale: Preserves protest and inclusion of captive king in asserted obedience.
verses.before: Saul said to Samuel, “I did listen to the voice of the LORD. I went on the way that the LORD sent me. I brought Agag king of Amalek, and Amalek I devoted to destruction.
verses.after: Saul answered Samuel, “But I did listen to the LORD’s voice! I went on the mission he sent me on. I brought back Agag king of Amalek and devoted Amalek to destruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul said to Samuel, “I did listen to the voice of the LORD. I went on the way that the LORD sent me. I brought Agag king of Amalek, and Amalek I devoted to destruction.

verses.rationale: Keeps attribution to troops and contradiction of devoted goods retained.
verses.before: But the people took from the spoil sheep and cattle, the best of what was devoted to destruction, to sacrifice to the LORD your God at Gilgal.”
verses.after: The troops took sheep and cattle from the plunder, the best of what was devoted to destruction, to sacrifice to the LORD your God at Gilgal.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But the people took from the spoil sheep and cattle, the best of what was devoted to destruction, to sacrifice to the LORD your God at Gilgal.”

verses.rationale: Keeps hearing/obedience semantic connection in verse-contained parallel lines.
verses.before: Samuel said: “Does the LORD delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as in listening to the voice of the LORD? Look, to listen is better than sacrifice, to pay attention than the fat of rams.
verses.after: Samuel said, “Does the LORD delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as much as in listening to his voice? Listen: obedience is better than sacrifice, attention better than the fat of rams.
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel said: “Does the LORD delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as in listening to the voice of the LORD? Look, to listen is better than sacrifice, to pay attention than the fat of rams.

verses.rationale: Retains teraphim concrete term through household gods and repeated rejection.
verses.before: For rebellion is like the sin of divination, and presumption like wickedness and idols. Because you rejected the word of the LORD, he has rejected you from being king.”
verses.after: Rebellion is like the sin of divination, and stubbornness like wickedness and household gods. Because you have rejected the LORD’s word, he has rejected you as king.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For rebellion is like the sin of divination, and presumption like wickedness and idols. Because you rejected the word of the LORD, he has rejected you from being king.”

verses.rationale: Keeps confession and competing voices as Saul’s stated cause.
verses.before: Saul said to Samuel, “I have sinned, for I transgressed the command of the LORD and your words because I feared the people and listened to their voice.
verses.after: Saul told Samuel, “I have sinned. I violated the LORD’s command and your words because I feared the people and listened to their voice.
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul said to Samuel, “I have sinned, for I transgressed the command of the LORD and your words because I feared the people and listened to their voice.

verses.rationale: Preserves forgiveness request to Samuel and accompanying worship.
verses.before: And now, please forgive my sin and return with me so that I may bow down to the LORD.”
verses.after: Now please forgive my sin and return with me so I can worship the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, please forgive my sin and return with me so that I may bow down to the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Keeps refusal and symmetrical rejection.
verses.before: Samuel said to Saul, “I will not return with you, for you rejected the word of the LORD, and the LORD has rejected you from being king over Israel.”
verses.after: Samuel answered, “I will not return with you. You have rejected the LORD’s word, and the LORD has rejected you as king over Israel.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel said to Saul, “I will not return with you, for you rejected the word of the LORD, and the LORD has rejected you from being king over Israel.”

verses.rationale: Clarifies Saul as seizing subject and Samuel’s robe from context.
verses.before: As Samuel turned to go, Saul seized the edge of his robe, and it tore.
verses.after: As Samuel turned to go, Saul seized the edge of his robe, and it tore.
verses.tsw_comparator: As Samuel turned to go, Saul seized the edge of his robe, and it tore.

verses.rationale: Preserves physical tear metaphor and unnamed fellow recipient.
verses.before: Samuel said to him, “The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today and has given it to your companion who is better than you.
verses.after: Samuel told him, “Today the LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel away from you and given it to someone near you who is better than you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel said to him, “The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today and has given it to your companion who is better than you.

verses.rationale: Retains title and nacham tension with vv11,35 rather than resolving doctrinally.
verses.before: And also the Glory of Israel does not lie or change his mind, for he is not a human being that he should change his mind.”
verses.after: The Glory of Israel does not lie or change his mind. He is not a human being who changes his mind.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And also the Glory of Israel does not lie or change his mind, for he is not a human being that he should change his mind.”

verses.rationale: Keeps public honor request and your God wording.
verses.before: Then Saul said, “I have sinned. Now please honor me before the elders of my people and before Israel, and return with me so that I may bow down to the LORD your God.”
verses.after: Saul said, “I have sinned. But please honor me before the elders of my people and before Israel. Return with me so I can worship the LORD your God.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Saul said, “I have sinned. Now please honor me before the elders of my people and before Israel, and return with me so that I may bow down to the LORD your God.”

verses.rationale: Preserves changed action without inventing reason for Samuel’s return.
verses.before: So Samuel returned after Saul, and Saul bowed down to the LORD.
verses.after: Samuel returned with Saul, and Saul worshiped the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Samuel returned after Saul, and Saul bowed down to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Uses confident/delicately approach reading, notes trembling alternative without changing speech into an unmarked inner thought.
verses.before: Samuel said, “Bring near to me Agag king of Amalek.” Agag came to him confidently. Agag said, “Surely the bitterness of death has turned aside.”
verses.after: Samuel said, “Bring me Agag king of Amalek.” Agag came to him confidently and said, “Surely the bitterness of death has passed.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel said, “Bring near to me Agag king of Amalek.” Agag came to him confidently. Agag said, “Surely the bitterness of death has turned aside.”

verses.rationale: Preserves maternal bereavement and dismemberment rather than vague execution.
verses.before: Yet Samuel said, “As your sword has made women childless, so will your mother be childless among women.” And Samuel cut Agag to pieces before the LORD at Gilgal.
verses.after: Samuel said, “As your sword has made women childless, so your mother will be childless among women.” Then Samuel cut Agag in pieces before the LORD at Gilgal.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Samuel said, “As your sword has made women childless, so shall your mother be childless among women.” And Samuel cut Agag to pieces before the LORD at Gilgal.

verses.rationale: Keeps separate departures and named places.
verses.before: Then Samuel went to Ramah, and Saul went up to his house at Gibeah of Saul.
verses.after: Samuel went to Ramah, and Saul went home to Gibeah of Saul.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Samuel went to Ramah, and Saul went up to his house at Gibeah of Saul.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated divine regret and Samuel mourning without harmonizing later encounter narrative.
verses.before: Samuel did not see Saul again until the day of his death, but Samuel mourned for Saul. And the LORD regretted that he had made Saul king over Israel.
verses.after: Samuel did not see Saul again until the day of his death, though he mourned for him. The LORD regretted making Saul king over Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel did not see Saul again until the day of his death, but Samuel mourned for Saul. And the LORD regretted that he had made Saul king over Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps mourning, horn and seeing language initiating selection theme.
verses.before: The LORD said to Samuel, “How long will you grieve over Saul, since I have rejected him from being king over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and go. I will send you to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for I have provided for myself a king among his sons.”
verses.after: The LORD said to Samuel, “How long will you mourn for Saul when I have rejected him as king over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and go. I am sending you to Jesse of Bethlehem; I have seen among his sons a king for myself.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Samuel, “How long will you grieve over Saul, since I have rejected him from being king over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and go. I will send you to Jesse the Bethlehemite, for I have provided for myself a king among his sons.”

verses.rationale: Preserves threat and limited disclosure without ethical explanation in text.
verses.before: Samuel said, “How can I go? If Saul hears of it, he will kill me.” And the LORD said, “Take a heifer with you and say, ‘I have come to sacrifice to the LORD.’”
verses.after: Samuel asked, “How can I go? Saul will hear and kill me.” The LORD answered, “Take a heifer with you and say, ‘I have come to sacrifice to the LORD.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel said, “How can I go? If Saul hears of it, he will kill me.” And the LORD said, “Take a heifer with you and say, ‘I have come to sacrifice to the LORD.’”

verses.rationale: Keeps deferred identification and divine choice.
verses.before: “Invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will show you what you will do. You will anoint for me the one whom I name to you.”
verses.after: Invite Jesse to the sacrifice. I will tell you what to do, and you will anoint for me the one I name to you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will show you what you shall do. You shall anoint for me the one whom I name to you.”

verses.rationale: Preserves fearful reception and peace question.
verses.before: Samuel did what the LORD commanded and came to Bethlehem. The elders of the city came trembling to meet him and said, “Do you come in peace?”
verses.after: Samuel did what the LORD said and came to Bethlehem. The elders of the town trembled as they met him. “Do you come in peace?” they asked.
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel did what the LORD commanded and came to Bethlehem. The elders of the city came trembling to meet him and said, “Do you come in peace?”

verses.rationale: Keeps self-consecration command and Samuel’s action with family.
verses.before: He said, “In peace. I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Consecrate yourselves and come with me to the sacrifice.” And he consecrated Jesse and his sons and invited them to the sacrifice.
verses.after: “In peace,” he answered. “I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Consecrate yourselves and come with me to the sacrifice.” He consecrated Jesse and his sons and invited them.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “In peace. I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Consecrate yourselves and come with me to the sacrifice.” And he consecrated Jesse and his sons and invited them to the sacrifice.

verses.rationale: Marks Samuel’s inference rather than divine identification.
verses.before: When they came, he looked on Eliab and thought, “Surely the LORD’s anointed is now before the LORD.”
verses.after: When they arrived, Samuel saw Eliab and thought, “Surely the LORD’s anointed stands here before him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When they came, he looked on Eliab and thought, “Surely the LORD’s anointed is now before the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Makes elliptical divine comparison explicit; preserves eyes/heart contrast and rejected stature.
verses.before: But the LORD said to Samuel, “Do not look on his appearance or on the height of his stature, because I have rejected him. For the LORD does not see as mortals see; they look on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart.”
verses.after: But the LORD told Samuel, “Do not look at his appearance or his height. I have rejected him. I do not see as people see. People look at what meets the eyes, but the LORD looks at the heart.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But the LORD said to Samuel, “Do not look on his appearance or on the height of his stature, because I have rejected him. For the LORD does not see as mortals see; they look on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart.”

verses.rationale: Keeps second son and repeated nonselection formula.
verses.before: Then Jesse called Abinadab and made him pass before Samuel. And he said, “The LORD has not chosen this one.”
verses.after: Jesse called Abinadab and had him pass before Samuel. Samuel said, “The LORD has not chosen this one either.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jesse called Abinadab and made him pass before Samuel. And he said, “The LORD has not chosen this one.”

verses.rationale: Retains deliberate repetition rather than compressing selection.
verses.before: Then Jesse made Shammah pass by. And he said, “The LORD has not chosen this one either.”
verses.after: Jesse then had Shammah pass by. Samuel said, “The LORD has not chosen this one either.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jesse made Shammah pass by. And he said, “The LORD has not chosen this one either.”

verses.rationale: Preserves total seven and collective denial.
verses.before: Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel, and Samuel said to Jesse, “The LORD has not chosen any of these.”
verses.after: Jesse had seven of his sons pass before Samuel. Samuel told him, “The LORD has chosen none of these.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel, and Samuel said to Jesse, “The LORD has not chosen any of these.”

verses.rationale: Keeps youngest’s absent labor and meal-delay sense of nasob with note.
verses.before: Samuel said to Jesse, “Are all your sons here?” And he said, “There remains yet the youngest, but he is keeping the sheep.” Samuel said to Jesse, “Send and bring him; for we will not sit down until he comes here.”
verses.after: Samuel asked Jesse, “Are these all the young men?” “The youngest is still out tending the flock,” he replied. Samuel said, “Send for him. We will not sit down until he gets here.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Samuel said to Jesse, “Are all your sons here?” And he said, “There remains yet the youngest, but he is keeping the sheep.” And Samuel said to Jesse, “Send and bring him; for we will not sit down until he comes here.”

verses.rationale: Retains physical description despite preceding warning; does not force ruddy to hair color.
verses.before: He sent and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with beautiful eyes, and handsome. And the LORD said, “Rise and anoint him, for this is the one.”
verses.after: Jesse sent for him and brought him in. He was ruddy, with beautiful eyes and a handsome appearance. The LORD said, “Get up and anoint him. He is the one.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He sent and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with beautiful eyes, and handsome. And the LORD said, “Rise and anoint him, for this is the one.”

verses.rationale: Keeps brothers present, first named David here and enduring Spirit statement.
verses.before: Then Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him among his brothers. And the spirit of the LORD came mightily upon David from that day forward. Samuel then set out and went to Ramah.
verses.after: Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him among his brothers. From that day onward the LORD’s Spirit rushed upon David. Then Samuel left for Ramah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers. And the spirit of the LORD came mightily upon David from that day forward. Samuel then set out and went to Ramah.

verses.rationale: Preserves harmful spirit’s divine source without diagnosis or demonic-system addition.
verses.before: Now the spirit of the LORD departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the LORD tormented him.
verses.after: The LORD’s Spirit departed from Saul, and a harmful spirit from the LORD tormented him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the spirit of the LORD departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the LORD tormented him.

verses.rationale: Keeps servants’ repeated explanation distinct from narrator.
verses.before: Saul’s servants said to him, “See now, an evil spirit from God is tormenting you.”
verses.after: Saul’s servants said to him, “A harmful spirit from God is tormenting you.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Saul’s servants said to him, “See now, an evil spirit from God is tormenting you.”

verses.rationale: Preserves proposed musical relief and lyre specificity.
verses.before: “Let our lord now command the servants who are before you to seek out someone who is skillful in playing the lyre. When the evil spirit from God is upon you, he will play it, and you will be well.”
verses.after: Let our lord command his servants here to find someone skilled at playing the lyre. When the harmful spirit from God comes upon you, he can play, and you will feel relief.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Let our lord now command the servants who are before you to seek out someone who is skillful in playing the lyre. When the evil spirit from God is upon you, he will play it, and you will be well.”

verses.rationale: Keeps direct request for skill.
verses.before: So Saul said to his servants, “Provide for me someone who can play well, and bring him to me.”
verses.after: Saul told his servants, “Find me someone who plays well and bring him to me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So Saul said to his servants, “Provide for me someone who can play well, and bring him to me.”

verses.rationale: Preserves servant’s full warrior description without harmonizing later youth portrayal.
verses.before: One of the young men answered, “I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite who is skillful in playing, a man of valor, a warrior, prudent in speech, and a man of good presence; and the LORD is with him.”
verses.after: One of the young men answered, “I have seen a son of Jesse of Bethlehem who knows how to play. He is a strong, capable man, a warrior, discerning in speech, and handsome. The LORD is with him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: One of the young men answered, “I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite who is skillful in playing, a man of valor, a warrior, prudent in speech, and a man of good presence; and the LORD is with him.”

verses.rationale: Keeps known name and current occupation.
verses.before: So Saul sent messengers to Jesse and said, “Send me your son David, who is with the sheep.”
verses.after: Saul sent messengers to Jesse: “Send me your son David, who is with the flock.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So Saul sent messengers to Jesse and said, “Send me your son David, who is with the sheep.”

verses.rationale: Uses donkey-load sense of compressed hamor lehem, retains three gifts.
verses.before: Jesse took a donkey laden with bread, a skin of wine, and a young goat, and sent them by his son David to Saul.
verses.after: Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread, a skin of wine, and one young goat and sent them to Saul with his son David.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jesse took a donkey laden with bread, a skin of wine, and a young goat, and sent them by his son David to Saul.

verses.rationale: Clarifies both pronoun referents and preserves love rather than mere approval.
verses.before: David came to Saul and entered his service. Saul loved him greatly, and he became his armor-bearer.
verses.after: David came to Saul and entered his service. Saul loved him greatly, and David became his armor-bearer.
verses.tsw_comparator: David came to Saul and entered his service. Saul loved him greatly, and he became his armor-bearer.

verses.rationale: Keeps permission request and favor language.
verses.before: Saul sent word to Jesse, saying, “Let David remain in my service, for he has found favor in my sight.”
verses.after: Saul sent word to Jesse, “Please let David remain in my service. He has found favor with me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Saul sent word to Jesse, saying, “Let David remain in my service, for he has found favor in my sight.”

verses.rationale: Keeps ruah/relief wordplay and episodic departure without claiming cure.
verses.before: And whenever the evil spirit from God came upon Saul, David took the lyre and played it with his hand. And Saul would be relieved and feel better, and the evil spirit would depart from him.
verses.after: Whenever the spirit from God came upon Saul, David took the lyre and played. Saul could breathe freely and felt better, and the harmful spirit left him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And whenever the evil spirit from God came upon Saul, David took the lyre and played it with his hand. And Saul would be relieved and feel better, and the evil spirit would depart from him.
